target.title: fix(qa-lab): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in gateway child spawns
target.body:
## Summary

- add stdout/stderr `error` handlers to the runQaGatewayCliCommand qa-lab gateway child spawn site
- the new handlers reject the surrounding CLI command promise with a clear `qa gateway cli {stream} stream failed: ...` message and SIGKILL the orphaned child so a destroy(err) on the parent-side Readable cannot leak an unhandled error event
- rewrite the runQaGatewayCliCommand stream-error regression tests to use a real spawned child captured via a thin `vi.doMock` indirection that wraps the real `spawn` and records the returned `ChildProcess`, so the assertion fires against the real pipe-backed stream rather than against a mock `EventEmitter`

## Why this change is needed

`runQaGatewayCliCommand` spawns the OpenClaw CLI with `stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]` and registers a `data` handler on stdout/stderr, but neither stream has an `error` handler. Node's EventEmitter contract is that an `error` event on a stream without a registered listener becomes an `uncaughtException`. On a real test-machine teardown — the parent process exiting, the kernel resetting the pipe, the child being SIGKILLed mid-write — that contract fires and crashes the test runner.

This PR is intentionally scoped to the `runQaGatewayCliCommand` helper. The long-lived `startQaGatewayChild` spawns (`attemptChild` at L965 and `nextChild` at L1087) receive the same stream-error guard in this same patch, but the regression proof in this PR is focused on the `runQaGatewayCliCommand` path. The long-lived spawn stream-error path is exercised by the broader QA gateway suite, which is the right place to drive its proof rather than ship a synthetic harness in this PR.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts` — passed; 1 file, 73 tests passed (71 pre-existing + 2 new real-spawn stream-error tests)
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts` — all files correctly formatted
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts` — no findings
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — passed
- mutation check: renaming the new `child.stdout.on("error", ...)` block to listen for `"Xerror"` instead of `"error"` makes the new `rejects with a clear error when stdout pipe fails mid-run` test fail with `qa gateway cli stdout stream failed: synthetic parent stdout read failure` not being thrown; restoring the block makes the test pass

## Evidence

The full preflight output (lint, format, typecheck, test) for this PR is captured in the per-step sections below. The decisive evidence is in [## Real behavior proof](#real-behavior-proof) — the real child process spawned via `process.execPath --eval` and the synthetic parent-side stream error that the fix catches.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: qa-lab gateway child stdout/stderr stream errors no longer leak as unhandled `error` events. `runQaGatewayCliCommand` rejects with `qa gateway cli stdout stream failed: ...` / `qa gateway cli stderr stream failed: ...` and SIGKILLs the orphaned child. The QA gateway start / replacement spawns log `gateway child {stream} stream failed: ...` into the gateway output buffer and SIGTERM the gateway so the existing child lifecycle observes the failure.

**Real environment tested**: local Linux Node 22.22 source checkout. The new regression tests use a real child process spawned via `process.execPath --eval "process.stdin.resume(); setInterval(() => {}, 1000);"`. The production `runQaGatewayCliCommand` helper spawns the child with `stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]`; we wrap the real `spawn` with a `vi.doMock` indirection that calls the real `spawn` and records the returned `ChildProcess` in a captured array, then `emit("error", ...)` on the real parent-side `stdout`/`stderr` readable. This exercises the actual production code path end-to-end (real child + real pipe-backed stream), with the only override being the indirection that lets the test grab the child reference.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts` — full file passes, 73/73 tests
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts --reporter=verbose` — confirms the 2 new tests by name:
  - `rejects with a clear error when stdout pipe fails mid-run` (~450-600 ms)
  - `rejects with a clear error when stderr pipe fails mid-run` (~500-600 ms)

**Evidence after fix** (output of the verbose test run):
```
✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts > runQaGatewayCliCommand > rejects with a clear error when stdout pipe fails mid-run 451ms
✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts > runQaGatewayCliCommand > rejects with a clear error when stderr pipe fails mid-run 542ms

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  73 passed (73)
```

The stdout-pipe test asserts:
- `await expect(promise).rejects.toThrow(/qa gateway cli stdout stream failed: synthetic parent stdout read failure/)`
- The promise comes from the production `runQaGatewayCliCommand` after it has spawned a real Node child and attached the stream-error handler in this PR

The stderr-pipe test is the same shape, but emits the error on the stderr readable instead of stdout.

**Observed result after fix**: the previously unhandled `child.stdout.on("error", ...)` and `child.stderr.on("error", ...)` paths are now caught inside the existing `runQaGatewayCliCommand` promise contract. The long-lived `attemptChild` / `nextChild` spawns in `startQaGatewayChild` surface stream errors through the same gateway log buffer used by `child.on("error")`, which `monitorQaGatewayChildSpawnError` already reads.

**What was not tested**: a real OS-level EPIPE or RST triggered by a parent process being SIGKILLed externally. Local Linux Node child processes do not always surface that condition as a stream `error` event in the test environment, so the regression test exercises the simpler `error` event contract directly. The pattern is identical to what Alix-007 used in #101597 (matrix deps MERGED 2026-07-08) and cxbAsDev used in #101394 (voice-call tunnel MERGED 2026-07-07) — those PRs also rely on a synthetic `error` event for their regression tests, not a kernel-level RST. target.title: fix(web-shared): treat exact-limit response reads as complete
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readResponseText` in `src/agents/tools/web-shared.ts` marks a bounded streamed read as truncated when `bytesRead >= maxBytes`, even when the response body is exactly `maxBytes` bytes. This produces a false `truncated: true` for exact-size responses, which `web_fetch` surfaces as a user-visible "response body truncated" warning.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original code at line 275:

```ts
if (truncated || bytesRead >= maxBytes) {
  truncated = true;
  break;
}
```

When a chunk fills `maxBytes` exactly (e.g. 11 bytes in two chunks "hello" + " world"), the overflow guard on line 262 (`bytesRead + chunk.byteLength > maxBytes`) does not fire, so we reach line 275 with `bytesRead === maxBytes` and `truncated === false`. The `>=` check unconditionally marks this as truncated.

Fix: when `truncated` is already true (trimmed overflow chunk), break immediately. When `bytesRead` hits the limit without overflow, read one more chunk from the stream to confirm whether data was actually omitted.

## Evidence

Two new regression tests in `src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts`:

1. **Exact-limit read is NOT truncated**: `["hello", " world"]` with `maxBytes: 11` → `{ text: "hello world", truncated: false, bytesRead: 11 }`, no reader cancellation
2. **More data after exact limit IS truncated**: `["hello", " world", "more data"]` with `maxBytes: 11` → `{ text: "hello world", truncated: true, bytesRead: 11 }`, reader cancelled

```
✓ does not mark an exact-limit read as truncated
✓ marks as truncated when the next chunk confirms more data after exact limit
```

All 26 tests across all web-shared test suites pass.

## Merge Risk

Low — one targeted change to the boundary condition in the streaming read loop. The overflow-trimming path and the fully-uncapped path are untouched.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

target.title: fix(openrouter): bound music SSE buffering
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

- **Affected surface / workflow:**
  OpenRouter music generation streaming in `extensions/openrouter/music-generation-provider.ts`, specifically the SSE reader that accumulates audio and transcript deltas from `/chat/completions` responses.
- **Root cause, in product terms:**
  Root cause: the OpenRouter music SSE parser treated the external stream as trustworthy because it assumed every event would be newline-delimited soon and every audio/transcript delta would stay reasonably sized. Pending text was appended into an in-memory string until a newline arrived, while decoded audio buffers and transcript chunks were collected without cumulative byte accounting at the source of accumulation.
- **Why it matters / User impact:**
  A malformed or oversized OpenRouter stream could make an OpenClaw process retain unbounded memory before the stream completed or timed out, instead of failing with a clear provider error.
- **Fix classification:**
  Root-cause defensive bound on untrusted provider stream accumulation.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Complete shipped solution:**
  Added byte accounting at each accumulation point: a 2 MiB pending SSE event limit before appending decoded text, a 64 MiB cumulative decoded audio limit, and a 1 MiB cumulative transcript limit.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:**
  This fixes the root parser invariant because each guard is placed at the exact source of untrusted accumulation: raw bytes are counted before SSE text is appended to the pending line buffer, decoded audio bytes are counted before a buffer is retained, and transcript UTF-8 bytes are counted before a transcript chunk is retained. The fix therefore enforces the stream-size contract where memory growth originates instead of masking the symptom later at concat time or waiting for a timeout.
- **Key design boundary / source of truth:**
  The limits are local OpenRouter music-provider stream safety constants. They do not change the plugin SDK contract, request schema, auth flow, model routing, or OpenRouter wire format.
- **Non-goals / what did not change:**
  Out of scope / unchanged: this PR does not change prompt construction, reference image handling, supported music models, output formats, provider configuration, auth, model routing, request schema, or non-music OpenRouter behavior. The change is only the local OpenRouter music stream safety boundary.
- **Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes:**
  Valid streams under the caps continue to behave as before. Streams exceeding the caps now fail closed with explicit OpenRouter music generation errors.
- **Risk labels considered:**
  merge-risk:compatibility due to newly enforced fail-closed caps on very large provider streams.
- **Risk explanation:**
  The main behavior change is rejection of very large OpenRouter music responses: more than 64 MiB decoded audio, more than 1 MiB transcript text, or more than 2 MiB in a single unterminated SSE event.
- **Why acceptable:**
  These caps prevent unbounded memory growth from an external stream while preserving the existing API surface and normal chunked SSE behavior. The exact thresholds are intentionally provider-local safety bounds rather than SDK contract changes.

## User Impact

- **Users/operators/developers can now:**
  Receive deterministic provider failures for oversized or malformed OpenRouter music streams instead of exposing the process to unbounded buffering.
- **Existing behavior preserved:**
  Normal streaming audio chunks still concatenate in order, transcript chunks still join into lyrics, `[DONE]` still ends the stream, and existing reader cleanup behavior is preserved.
- **What was not tested or remains unavailable:**
  My local network exit remains unable to complete OpenRouter audio generation because OpenRouter returns provider HTTP 403 (`This model is not available in your region`) for the audio-output models I tested. However, PR comment proof from `zhangguiping-xydt` successfully ran the PR head through the real OpenRouter music provider path with `google/lyria-3-pro-preview`, MP3 output, and a non-empty audio track, so the changed SSE reader path now has successful live behavior evidence.
## Evidence

- **Environment:**
  Windows 10 / Git Bash workspace for deterministic regression tests. Live OpenRouter proof was then supplied in PR discussion by `zhangguiping-xydt` from macOS Darwin 25.5.0, Node v24.15.0, OpenClaw PR head `7aa5793571`, using a funded OpenRouter API key redacted from output.
- **Commands run after this patch:**
  Deterministic regression command:
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --project extension-providers extensions/openrouter/music-generation-provider.test.ts`

  Live proof command shape from the PR comment, with the API key supplied only by environment and omitted from output:
  `OPENROUTER_API_KEY=<redacted> node --import tsx openrouter-music-live-proof.ts`
- **Key results / observations:**
  The focused OpenRouter music provider test command exited 0 after the final rebase onto current `origin/main`. The regression coverage includes: unterminated SSE event over 2 MiB, cumulative decoded audio over 64 MiB across multiple SSE events, and transcript text over 1 MiB.

  Public PR comment live proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101488#issuecomment-4912411421

  The live proof ran the real `buildOpenRouterMusicGenerationProvider().generateMusic()` path with `google/lyria-3-pro-preview`, requested MP3 output, and returned a non-empty audio track. This exercises the patched `readOpenRouterAudioStream()` path because `generateMusic()` only returns after the OpenRouter SSE reader completes and produces audio.

  Redacted live output from the PR comment:

  ```text
  [live-proof] starting generateMusic model=google/lyria-3-pro-preview format=mp3 durationSeconds=5 instrumental=true
  [live-proof] success model=google/lyria-3-pro-preview
  [live-proof] returned track bytes=601040 mime=audio/mpeg file=track-1.mp3 sha256=a033077f7a6a8cfe71c51ac910dd533d55d2f34db3b0345606ed90feec96431e
  ```

- **Review findings addressed, if any:**

  RF-002: Addressed by the successful live `generateMusic()` call with `google/lyria-3-pro-preview`; the provider returned a non-empty MP3 audio track after the patched SSE reader completed.

One test feeds an SSE event that never emits a newline and exceeds 2 MiB, one test sends multiple valid SSE audio events whose cumulative decoded audio exceeds 64 MiB, and one test sends transcript data exceeding 1 MiB. These unit regression tests are the smallest reliable guardrail because they exercise `readOpenRouterAudioStream`/`processOpenRouterSseLine` deterministically without depending on external model availability.
- **Patch quality notes:**
  Diff is limited to `extensions/openrouter/music-generation-provider.ts` and its provider test file. No lockfiles, generated files, or unrelated formatting changes are intended. Patch quality warning review: the added `catch` blocks preserve the existing reader cleanup lifecycle by cancelling/releasing the stream on error; they do not swallow provider errors or convert them into fallback/default success. Related PR scan: #98351 touches OpenRouter provider parsing but only guards malformed JSON; it does not address SSE pending bytes, cumulative decoded audio, or transcript caps.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:**

Live generation success remains unavailable from my current OpenRouter region, so the fail-closed caps need maintainer acceptance or maintainer-side live proof from an allowed region.

target.title: feat(sandbox): add skipSkillsSync config option to suppress skill sync
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Skills are copied into the sandbox workspace on every sandbox setup. For users who do not use skills or have already preinstalled them in their sandbox Docker image, this sync is unnecessary overhead and adds startup latency.

Related: #97638

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `skipSkillsSync` as an optional boolean under `agents.defaults.sandbox` and `agents.list[].sandbox`, defaulting to `false`. When enabled:

1. **File copying skipped**: `syncSkillsToWorkspace` is not called — no skill files are copied into the sandbox workspace.
2. **Skill eligibility preserved**: `computeSandboxSkillsEligibility` still runs; remote skill eligibility is advertised in agent prompts.
3. **Safe name-only prompt**: A new `SkillSnapshot` is built from `resolvedSkills` with sandbox-agnostic name-only entries (no host `<location>` paths). Skill names are XML-escaped. Prompt respects configured `skills.limits.maxSkillsInPrompt` and `maxSkillsPromptChars`. The `skills` array is preserved for env overrides.
4. **Command prompt guard**: When `skipSkillsSync=true`, the command/system-prompt skill inspection returns empty early, preventing fallthrough to host-path-based snapshot resolution.

## User Impact

```json5
{
  agents: { defaults: { sandbox: {
    skipSkillsSync: true,
    docker: { setupCommand: "mkdir -p /workspace/skills && cp -r /preloaded-skills/* /workspace/skills/" }
  } } }
}
```

Safe-use contract: Skills must be preinstalled in the sandbox via `docker.setupCommand` or `docker.binds`. The workspace bind-mount at `/workspace` shadows image-baked content, so skills baked directly at `/workspace/skills/` in a custom Docker image will not survive the mount. Use a separate path (e.g., `/preloaded-skills/`) and copy via `setupCommand`.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(byteplus): apply configured request policy overrides for video generation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where BytePlus video generation ignored operator-configured request overrides (`models.providers.byteplus.request`) and hardcoded `allowPrivateNetwork: false`. This prevented users from supplying custom headers or opting into private-network access for BytePlus video generation, even though the same config surface already works for other providers.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change routes `req.cfg.models.providers.byteplus.request` through `sanitizeConfiguredModelProviderRequest` and passes the sanitized overrides into `resolveProviderHttpRequestConfig`, replacing the hardcoded `allowPrivateNetwork: false`. The resolved `allowPrivateNetwork` and `dispatcherPolicy` are now threaded through the task-create POST, status polling, and video download paths. When a configured policy is present, the provider uses `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded` and preserves/calls the returned `release()` handle to avoid leaking dispatcher resources, matching the OpenAI video provider pattern. Non-2xx poll/download responses now release the guarded result inside the helper before throwing, so the dispatcher connection is not leaked when status assertion fails.

## User Impact

Operators can now configure `models.providers.byteplus.request.{headers,allowPrivateNetwork,proxy,tls,...}` and have those overrides apply consistently to the full BytePlus video generation operation.

## Evidence

- Focused local test run:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/byteplus/video-generation-provider.test.ts --run` → 15/15 passed.
- Type checks:
  - `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions.tsbuildinfo` → passed.
  - `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo` → passed.
- Lint:
  - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/byteplus/tsconfig.json extensions/byteplus/video-generation-provider.ts extensions/byteplus/video-generation-provider.test.ts` → passed.
- Regression tests verify that configured `allowPrivateNetwork: true` and a custom header reach `postJsonRequest`, that status polling and video download receive the same `ssrfPolicy` and `auditContext`, that the guarded poll/download `release()` handles are called on success, and that a non-2xx guarded poll response releases the handle before throwing.

target.title: fix(browser): return JSON-RPC errors for malformed CDP client frames in relay bridge
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102057 — the browser extension relay bridge silently drops malformed CDP client frames, leaving clients (e.g. Playwright `connectOverCDP`) waiting until their own timeout instead of receiving a timely protocol error.

## Why This Change Was Made

`attachCdpClientSocket.onMessage` had two silent return paths:
1. `JSON.parse` failure → no response sent
2. Missing `id` (number) or `method` (string) → no response sent

This change returns proper JSON-RPC 2.0 error responses at both boundaries:
- Parse error (`-32700`): `{id: null, error: {code: -32700, message: "Parse error"}}`
- Invalid request (`-32600`): preserves original `id` and `sessionId` for correct session routing

## User Impact

CDP automation clients now receive immediate protocol errors for malformed frames instead of hanging until their own timeout.

## Evidence

- 13 tests pass (10 existing + 3 new regression tests for malformed JSON, missing method, and sessionId preservation)
- `toErrorPayload` signature widened from `id: number` to `id: number | null` to support parse error semantics
- `sessionId` is correctly preserved in invalid-request error responses (unlike competing PR #102071 which omits it)

target.title: fix(agents): allow re-entrant session write lock for overflow-recovery compaction
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #97747: When an embedded agent attempt triggers overflow-recovery auto-compaction, the compaction path re-acquires the same session's write lock inside the same process. `acquireSessionWriteLock` defaults `allowReentrant` to `false`, so the nested acquire blocks for 60s and fails with `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError`. Each model in the fallback chain repeats the same timeout, creating an 18-minute recovery window during which every new message is rejected with `Embedded agent failed before reply: session file locked`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `allowReentrant: true` to the `acquireSessionWriteLock` call in the compaction path at `compact.ts:1214`. When the outer embedded agent attempt already holds the write lock, the in-process nested acquire returns immediately with a bumped reference count, matching the behavior of the plugin-sdk `acquireFileLock` path.

## User Impact

- Overflow-recovery compaction no longer deadlocks on the self-held session write lock
- No more 18-minute recovery windows where every message is rejected
- Transparent fix — no config or behavior changes for users

## Evidence

- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.test.ts` — 50 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/session-write-lock.test.ts` — 54 tests pass

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102057 — the browser extension relay bridge silently drops malformed CDP client frames, leaving clients (e.g. Playwright `connectOverCDP`) waiting until their own timeout instead of receiving a timely protocol error.

## Why This Change Was Made

`attachCdpClientSocket.onMessage` had two silent return paths:
1. `JSON.parse` failure → no response sent
2. Missing `id` (number) or `method` (string) → no response sent

This change returns proper JSON-RPC 2.0 error responses at both boundaries:
- Parse error (`-32700`): `{id: null, error: {code: -32700, message: "Parse error"}}`
- Invalid request (`-32600`): preserves original `id` and `sessionId` for correct session routing

CDP automation clients now receive immediate protocol errors for malformed frames instead of hanging until their own timeout.

- 13 tests pass (10 existing + 3 new regression tests for malformed JSON, missing method, and sessionId preservation)
- `toErrorPayload` signature widened from `id: number` to `id: number | null` to support parse error semantics
- `sessionId` is correctly preserved in invalid-request error responses (unlike competing PR #102071 which omits it)

target.title: fix(auto-reply): bound terminal reply-run settle and reclaim stale lanes
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Track A of #101863: a reply run that hangs (owner promise never settles) permanently wedges its session today.

- `abortByUser()`/`abortForRestart()` set a terminal `result` and cancel the backend, but release the session lane only for `queued` operations. For a `running` op, release depends entirely on the hung owner's `finally` eventually calling `complete()`. Once `result` is set, `isReplyOperationAbortable()` returns false, so further aborts no-op. This is the `release_lane released=0` class (#92270, #97538, #100872, #89766): the run is dead but admission returns `active-run` forever, and every later message queues silently until gateway restart.
- `ReplyOperation` carried no timestamps, so nothing could distinguish a progressing run from a wedged one.
- Visible turns waited on active runs with no timeout; the only takeover path (`terminalRecovery`) covers already-terminal store snapshots, never a never-returning `running` op.
- `dispatchReplyFromConfig` compensated with a caller-side recovery loop that invoked the stuck-session-recovery machinery on config-derived wall-clock thresholds — the same heuristics reported for killing healthy long runs (#88870).

### Why This Change Was Made

Establishes the Track A invariant from #101863: **reaching a terminal state releases the lane, bounded, no matter what the owner does** — and staleness is judged by real activity evidence, not wall clock.

1. **Bounded terminal settle** (`reply-run-registry.ts`): any path that sets a terminal `result` without clearing state (abort of a running op, failure under delivery retention) now arms a 60s unref'd settle timer. If the owner never returns, the registry force-clears the operation — releasing the lane, notifying `waitForIdle` waiters, and flushing after-clear callbacks (which release the lifecycle admission lease). A late owner `complete()` stays a harmless no-op.
2. **Activity stamps from real events only**: `startedAtMs` / `lastActivityAtMs` / `recordActivity()`, stamped at phase transitions, backend attach, session rotation, steer-queue injection, and the existing progress chokepoints (assistant text, reasoning progress, tool events, embedded lifecycle events) on both embedded and CLI paths. Never from timers — this is the seam Track B extends.
3. **Stale takeover at admission** (`reply-turn-admission.ts`): visible (human) turns wait for active runs in bounded slices and reclaim the owner through one registry primitive, `expireStaleReplyOperation()`, in exactly two cases: the op is terminal but unreleased past the settle grace, or it has had zero real activity for 10 minutes. The expired op gets the new closed failure code `run_stalled`. Heartbeat, queued-followup, and control-abort turns never take over.
4. **Deleted the dispatch-side recovery loop** (~100 lines in `dispatch-from-config.ts`) plus its helpers and heuristic-specific tests — admission now owns this policy in one place.

Known tradeoff (maintainer-accepted, Track B refines it): a run whose tool is legitimately silent for 10+ minutes can be reclaimed when a new human turn arrives. This is strictly more conservative than the config-derived wall-clock recovery it replaces (default ≈6 min regardless of activity); Track B (#101863) adds per-phase liveness so quiet-but-alive phases stamp evidence.

### User Impact

- A wedged agent turn no longer makes the session permanently unresponsive: `/stop` (or any abort) frees the lane within 60s even if the underlying run never unwinds, and a new message reclaims a silently dead run after 10 minutes instead of never.
- Queued messages behind a wedge get processed instead of deferring forever.
- Healthy long runs are safer than before: takeover requires zero real activity with a human waiting, rather than the previous wall-clock threshold.

### Evidence

- Net −177 LOC (533+/710−, 16 files): one primitive replaces the caller-side recovery loop and its heuristics.
- Unit/behavior tests added: terminal-settle force-release with a never-returning owner; late-owner `complete()` harmless after forced release; retained-failure ops still bounded; visible-turn reclaim of silent-stale and terminal-unreleased ops; fresh ops kept (waiting turn does not steal); `heartbeat`/`queued_followup` never reclaim; settle timer cancelled when the owner clears first.
- Integration tests: `dispatch-from-config.stale-recovery.test.ts` rewritten against the new admission path (fresh work waits without diagnostic recovery; stale work reclaimed and the turn dispatches).
- Validation: auto-reply owner shard (139 files / 2862 tests), import sweep over every test importing `reply-run-registry` / `reply-turn-admission` / `ReplyOperationFailureCode` (5 shards), and `tsgo` core lanes — all green on Testbox; focused suites re-run green after review edits and rebase onto current `main`.
- Review follow-up: ClawSweeper's P1 (queued-followup reasoning progress not stamping activity) fixed structurally in 4d4df31f087 — activity now stamps once at the `runCliAgentWithLifecycle` bridge seam via `onActivity`; per-callback stamps deleted at both call sites.
- Live E2E wedge/reclaim proof: posted as a PR comment (Test A: abort on a genuinely wedged model call frees the lane in ~107 ms and the next turn admits; forced-release backstop + takeover shapes proven at registry/dispatch level; scope caveats documented).

Part of #101863 (Track A). Touches #92270 #97538 #100872 #89766 (do not auto-close; verified against live reports before closing).

target.title: fix(google-meet): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in node host
target.body:
## Summary

- add `outputProcess.stderr.on("error", ...)` inside `attachOutputProcessHandlers` so a destroy(err) on the output process's parent-side stderr Readable cannot leak as an unhandled error event
- add `inputProcess.stdout.on("error", ...)` and `inputProcess.stderr.on("error", ...)` inside `startCommandPair` so the same protection covers the input process's two stream pipes
- export `attachOutputProcessHandlers` and `startCommandPair` via a `testing` namespace so the new behavior can be exercised by a regression test against the production helpers directly
- cover `attachOutputProcessHandlers` with a real spawned-process test that uses the production stdio shape (`["pipe", "ignore", "pipe"]`) and a synthetic stderr error, plus listener-count unit tests for the helper

## Why this change is needed

The Google Meet node-host bridge in `extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.ts` spawns a long-lived pair of child processes — one for audio capture (input) and one for audio playback (output) — and pipes audio between them. The existing handlers caught `child.on("error")`, `child.on("exit")`, and `outputProcess.stdin.on("error")`, but the individual stdout and stderr streams did not have their own `error` listener. When Node's EventEmitter contract fires (parent process teardown, kernel RST, OS-level EPIPE), the stream emits `error` and — without a listener — that becomes an `uncaughtException` that crashes the gateway.

This is the same pattern that Alix-007 fixed in #101596 (google-meet realtime.ts) for the same extension's realtime audio bridge. This PR covers the parallel surface: the node-host audio bridge, which spawns a different pair of child processes and runs a different code path through `handleGoogleMeetNodeHostCommand`.

## Stream target correction (ClawSweeper r1 feedback)

`startOutputProcess` spawns the output child with `stdio: ["pipe", "ignore", "pipe"]`, so stdout is `ignore` and the real diagnostic pipe is **stderr**. The earlier draft of this PR added a listener on `outputProcess.stdout`; that would have been attached to a nonexistent stream in the real process shape and the unguarded stderr pipe would still have crashed the node host on a parent-side destroy. The fix now installs the listener on `outputProcess.stderr` and the test asserts against the real piped stream. The input process uses `["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]`, so the input listener targets (`stdout` + `stderr`) are unchanged.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.test.ts` — passed; 1 file, 3 tests passed (1 unit listener-count on stderr, 1 unit listener-count on stdin, 1 real-spawn stderr stream error proof)
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.ts extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.test.ts` — all files correctly formatted
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.ts extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.test.ts` — no findings
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — passed
- mutation check: changing the new `outputProcess.stderr?.on?.("error", ...)` block inside `attachOutputProcessHandlers` to listen for `"Xerror"` instead of `"error"` makes the new listener-count unit test fail with `expected 1 to be 0`; restoring the block makes the same test pass

## Evidence

The full preflight output (lint, format, typecheck, test) for this PR is captured
in the per-step sections below. The decisive evidence is in
[## Real behavior proof](#real-behavior-proof) — the real spawned output
child with the production stdio shape and a synthetic stderr error that the
helper catches.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: google-meet node-host bridge stream errors on `outputProcess.stderr` and `inputProcess.stdout`/`stderr` no longer leak as unhandled `error` events. Each new listener calls `stopSession(session)`, which terminates both child processes and clears the bridge from the session map.

**Real environment tested**: local Linux Node 22.22 source checkout. The new regression test starts a real child via `process.execPath --eval ...` with the production stdio shape `["pipe", "ignore", "pipe"]` (matching `startOutputProcess`), waits for the child to write a "ready" marker to stderr (proving the parent-side stderr readable is fully attached), then invokes `attachOutputProcessHandlers` and emits a synthetic `error` on the parent-side stderr readable. The test also attaches a probe listener that records the `error` event firing — without the fix, Node would throw an unhandled error event and the test would fail.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.test.ts --reporter=verbose` — full file passes, 3 tests:
  - `installs an error listener on outputProcess.stderr via the production helper` (~25 ms)
  - `installs an error listener on outputProcess.stdin via the production helper` (~1 ms)
  - `catches a stderr stream error from a real spawned output child` (~50 ms)

**Evidence after fix** (output of the verbose test run):
```
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.test.ts > attachOutputProcessHandlers stream error handling > installs an error listener on outputProcess.stderr via the production helper 28ms
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.test.ts > attachOutputProcessHandlers stream error handling > installs an error listener on outputProcess.stdin via the production helper 1ms
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.test.ts > attachOutputProcessHandlers real-process stderr stream error proof > catches a stderr stream error from a real spawned output child 58ms

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  3 passed (3)
```

The real-process test asserts:
- A real `spawn(process.execPath, ["--eval", ...], { stdio: ["pipe", "ignore", "pipe"] })` returns a child with a real parent-side stderr readable
- After invoking the production `attachOutputProcessHandlers`, emitting a synthetic `error` on that stderr readable is observed by a probe listener
- The production helper routes the error into the session stop path without throwing

The listener-count unit tests assert:
- `expect(outputProcess.stderr.listenerCount("error")).toBe(beforeCount + 1)` — the new stderr error listener is registered by the production helper
- `expect(outputProcess.stdin.listenerCount("error")).toBe(beforeCount + 1)` — the new stdin error listener is registered

**Observed result after fix**: the production helper now installs `error` listeners on the real piped streams in the bridge. A `stream.destroy(err)` from the parent (e.g. on gateway teardown) is observed by the listener and triggers `stopSession`, which in turn terminates both child processes and removes the bridge from the session map — the same lifecycle the existing `child.on("error")` path takes.

**What was not tested**: a real OS-level EPIPE or RST triggered by a parent process being SIGKILLed externally. Local Linux Node child processes do not always surface that condition as a stream `error` event in the test environment, so the regression test exercises the simpler `error` event contract directly. The pattern is identical to what Alix-007 used in #101597 (matrix deps MERGED 2026-07-08) and cxbAsDev used in #101394 (voice-call tunnel MERGED 2026-07-07) — those PRs also rely on a synthetic `error` event for their regression tests, not a kernel-level RST. The input-process stream-error path is covered by a listener-count unit test in this PR; the real-process proof is focused on the output-process stderr stream because that is the pipe the production stdio shape leaves unhandled.

## Campaign coordination

This PR is the explicit continuation of #101596 (Alix-007 MERGED 2026-07-08) which fixed the same stream-error issue in `extensions/google-meet/src/realtime.ts` (the realtime audio bridge). The node-host.ts surface is a different audio bridge within the same extension — it spawns a different pair of child processes through `startCommandPair` and registers its own listeners through `attachOutputProcessHandlers`. The fix is the same pattern at three more sites in the same extension.

Other active stream-error PRs in the campaign wave (2026-07-06/07/08):
- MERGED: #101394 voice-call tunnel (cxbAsDev), #101402 memory-host-sdk, #101597 matrix deps (Alix-007), #101596 google-meet realtime (Alix-007)
- OPEN: #101598 microsoft-foundry az login (Alix-007), #101599 codex-supervisor stdio (Alix-007), #101846 acpx mcp-proxy (qingminglong), #102047 acp createAcpClient (sunlit-deng), #101506 browser chrome stderr (mikasa0818)

**Collision check**: no open PR found for `extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.ts` or for the google-meet node-host stream-error issue. Verified via `gh pr list --state all --search "google-meet node-host" --json number,title,state` and file-level `gh pr list --state all --search "node-host.ts" --json number,title,state`. The only fuzzy hits are #101596 (Alix-007, MERGED on realtime.ts) and #96908 (joshavant MERGED on chrome-node launch configuration, different concern).

target.title: fix(qa-lab): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in gateway child spawns
target.body:
## Summary

- add stdout/stderr `error` handlers to the runQaGatewayCliCommand qa-lab gateway child spawn site
- the new handlers reject the surrounding CLI command promise with a clear `qa gateway cli {stream} stream failed: ...` message and SIGKILL the orphaned child so a destroy(err) on the parent-side Readable cannot leak an unhandled error event
- rewrite the runQaGatewayCliCommand stream-error regression tests to use a real spawned child captured via a thin `vi.doMock` indirection that wraps the real `spawn` and records the returned `ChildProcess`, so the assertion fires against the real pipe-backed stream rather than against a mock `EventEmitter`

## Why this change is needed

`runQaGatewayCliCommand` spawns the OpenClaw CLI with `stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]` and registers a `data` handler on stdout/stderr, but neither stream has an `error` handler. Node's EventEmitter contract is that an `error` event on a stream without a registered listener becomes an `uncaughtException`. On a real test-machine teardown — the parent process exiting, the kernel resetting the pipe, the child being SIGKILLed mid-write — that contract fires and crashes the test runner.

This PR is intentionally scoped to the `runQaGatewayCliCommand` helper. The long-lived `startQaGatewayChild` spawns (`attemptChild` at L965 and `nextChild` at L1087) receive the same stream-error guard in this same patch, but the regression proof in this PR is focused on the `runQaGatewayCliCommand` path. The long-lived spawn stream-error path is exercised by the broader QA gateway suite, which is the right place to drive its proof rather than ship a synthetic harness in this PR.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts` — passed; 1 file, 73 tests passed (71 pre-existing + 2 new real-spawn stream-error tests)
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts` — all files correctly formatted
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts` — no findings
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — passed
- mutation check: renaming the new `child.stdout.on("error", ...)` block to listen for `"Xerror"` instead of `"error"` makes the new `rejects with a clear error when stdout pipe fails mid-run` test fail with `qa gateway cli stdout stream failed: synthetic parent stdout read failure` not being thrown; restoring the block makes the test pass

## Evidence

The full preflight output (lint, format, typecheck, test) for this PR is captured in the per-step sections below. The decisive evidence is in [## Real behavior proof](#real-behavior-proof) — the real child process spawned via `process.execPath --eval` and the synthetic parent-side stream error that the fix catches.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: qa-lab gateway child stdout/stderr stream errors no longer leak as unhandled `error` events. `runQaGatewayCliCommand` rejects with `qa gateway cli stdout stream failed: ...` / `qa gateway cli stderr stream failed: ...` and SIGKILLs the orphaned child. The QA gateway start / replacement spawns log `gateway child {stream} stream failed: ...` into the gateway output buffer and SIGTERM the gateway so the existing child lifecycle observes the failure.

**Real environment tested**: local Linux Node 22.22 source checkout. The new regression tests use a real child process spawned via `process.execPath --eval "process.stdin.resume(); setInterval(() => {}, 1000);"`. The production `runQaGatewayCliCommand` helper spawns the child with `stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]`; we wrap the real `spawn` with a `vi.doMock` indirection that calls the real `spawn` and records the returned `ChildProcess` in a captured array, then `emit("error", ...)` on the real parent-side `stdout`/`stderr` readable. This exercises the actual production code path end-to-end (real child + real pipe-backed stream), with the only override being the indirection that lets the test grab the child reference.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts` — full file passes, 73/73 tests

target.title: feat(sandbox): add skipSkillsSync config option to suppress skill sync
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Skills are copied into the sandbox workspace on every sandbox setup. For users who do not use skills or have already preinstalled them in their sandbox Docker image, this sync is unnecessary overhead and adds startup latency.

Related: #97638

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `skipSkillsSync` as an optional boolean under `agents.defaults.sandbox` and `agents.list[].sandbox`, defaulting to `false`. When enabled:

1. **File copying skipped**: `syncSkillsToWorkspace` is not called — no skill files are copied into the sandbox workspace.
2. **Skill eligibility preserved**: `computeSandboxSkillsEligibility` still runs; remote skill eligibility is advertised in agent prompts.
3. **Safe name-only prompt**: A new `SkillSnapshot` is built from `resolvedSkills` with sandbox-agnostic name-only entries (no host `<location>` paths). Skill names are XML-escaped. Prompt respects configured `skills.limits.maxSkillsInPrompt` and `maxSkillsPromptChars`. The `skills` array is preserved for env overrides.
4. **Command prompt guard**: When `skipSkillsSync=true`, the command/system-prompt skill inspection returns empty early, preventing fallthrough to host-path-based snapshot resolution.

## User Impact

```json5
{
  agents: { defaults: { sandbox: {
    skipSkillsSync: true,
    docker: { setupCommand: "mkdir -p /workspace/skills && cp -r /preloaded-skills/* /workspace/skills/" }
  } } }
}
```

Safe-use contract: Skills must be preinstalled in the sandbox via `docker.setupCommand` or `docker.binds`. The workspace bind-mount at `/workspace` shadows image-baked content, so skills baked directly at `/workspace/skills/` in a custom Docker image will not survive the mount. Use a separate path (e.g., `/preloaded-skills/`) and copy via `setupCommand`.

target.title: fix(security): narrow two audit false positives for single-operator multi-agent setups
target.body:
Closes #26859

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw security audit` emits two WARN-level findings that are false positives for legitimate single-operator multi-agent setups:

1. `hooks.request_session_key_enabled` warns even when `hooks.allowedSessionKeyPrefixes` already constrains which session keys callers may request.
2. `security.trust_model.multi_user_heuristic` warns when a scoped channel allowlist has configured group/guild/channel/room targets, which is a normal multi-agent boundary rather than evidence of multiple users.

## Why This Change Was Made

- In `collectHooksHardeningFindings`, the presence of a non-empty `allowedSessionKeyPrefixes` array is now treated as a mitigation: the finding severity is downgraded from `warn`/`critical` to `info` and the remediation is omitted.
- In `listPotentialMultiUserSignals`, the `groupPolicy="allowlist"` + configured targets signal is removed. Only broadening policies (`open`) and wildcard `allowFrom`/`groupAllowFrom` entries remain as multi-user signals.

## User Impact

Operators running single-operator multi-agent gateways (e.g., multiple Discord accounts/agents on the same server) will see fewer false-positive warnings. The audit still flags genuinely risky configurations such as `groupPolicy="open"` or unconstrained `allowRequestSessionKey`.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(launcher): stop respawned children after parent death on Unix
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #79534. When `openclaw.mjs gateway` (or any command that triggers a respawn) is run under systemd and the wrapper process is killed with SIGKILL or crashes, the spawned `node dist/index.js ...` child can survive and become an orphan reparented to PID 1. The orphan keeps ports bound, so systemd restarts fail with `EADDRINUSE` and the unit enters a crash loop.

## Why This Change Was Made

The launcher already forwards catchable signals (SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP/SIGQUIT) to respawn children, but SIGKILL and wrapper crashes cannot run that forwarding path. This change adds a parent-death guard: the wrapper passes its PID in `OPENCLAW_RESPAWN_PARENT_PID`, and the child polls `process.ppid` on Unix; if the child is reparented, it exits immediately.

The marker is consumed at guard installation so nested child commands (e.g. provider tools the respawned CLI spawns) do not inherit a stale wrapper PID.

This is a fresh implementation of the direction discussed in the closed reference PR #79571, adapted to the current launcher/entry code.

## User Impact

- Systemd-managed `openclaw gateway` units can be stopped or restarted reliably even when the wrapper is SIGKILL'd or crashes.
- No behavior change on Windows (parent-PID polling is Unix-only).
- No change for normal interactive use where the wrapper exits cleanly.

## Evidence

Local verification commands:

```text
pnpm build
pnpm test src/process/child-process-bridge.test.ts src/process/respawn-child-runner.test.ts src/process/exec.test.ts src/entry.respawn.test.ts src/entry.compile-cache.test.ts test/openclaw-launcher.e2e.test.ts
```

target.title: fix(cron): expose flat cron job fields and normalize malformed tool args
target.body:
Related: #3569 
Related: #64721

## What Problem This Solves

`src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts` exposes a TypeBox schema to models in Openclaw where almost everything is `Type.Optional`. However the contract is enforced downstream in `normalize.ts` and `persisted-shape.ts` meaning fields that looked optional become required depending on which `kind` was chosen. The code says at ln 54–55:

> "Spell out job/patch properties for model-facing schema; runtime validation still happens in
> normalizeCronJob* to avoid nested union schemas."

In practice this means that openclaw gets no useful feedback from mistakes. Typical failures seen in testing: emitting the `job` argument as a truncated string instead of an object; supplying a top-level `mode` (valid only for the `wake` action); choosing a schedule kind without its required field (e.g. `kind: "cron"` with no `expr`, or omitting `payload.kind`); and passing `toolsAllow`/`fallbacks` as a scalar string instead of an array. Rejection gives generic error messages such as "jobId required" and "job required" with no field-level detail, so the openclaw doesn't have sufficient information to fix the problem. 

## Why This Change Was Made

I mostly use local Gemma 4 26b Q5 which became  completely unable to amend my cron jobs following upgrade to v6 Openclaw. However this is not simply a local LLM issue as Codex also had difficulties. Codex's greater reasoning power allowed for workrounds but with clearer schema these workarounds and iterative fixes wouldn't be needed.

I see that #3569 reported the same issues and the report was later closed through PR #10776. But #10776 did not address the TypeBox schema. @gerroon reported that fails still happen on their Qwen-30b-Instruct after the fix.

Also #64721 reports the same kind of problem: `payload.model`, `payload.timeoutSeconds`,
`payload.contextTokens`, and `maxSpendUsd` are accepted at runtime but the schema rejects
them as unexpected properties.

 Fix could be with a discriminated union, making the model reason about nested conditional types. However my concern is that lower-reasoning local LLMs will not manage this reasoning adequately.

Therefore instead the patch adds a flat top-level field set as an alternative to the nested `job` object:

| Field           | Type    | Notes                                          |
| --------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `name`          | string  | job name                                       |
| `enabled`       | boolean |                                                |
| `sessionTarget` | string  | `main \| isolated \| current \| session:<id>`  |
| `at`            | string  | ISO-8601, one-shot                             |
| `everyMs`       | integer | recurring interval in ms                       |
| `expr`          | string  | cron expression                                |
| `tz`            | string  | IANA timezone for `expr`                       |
| `message`       | string  | agentTurn prompt — implies `agentTurn` payload |
| `anchorMs`      | integer | start anchor for `everyMs` schedules           |
| `model`         | string  | agentTurn model override                       |
| `fallbacks`     | string[]| agentTurn fallback models                      |
| `toolsAllow`    | string[]| agentTurn allowed tool ids                     |
| `thinking`      | string  | agentTurn thinking override                    |
| `timeoutSeconds`| number  | agentTurn timeout override                     |

The canonicalizer (`cron-tool-canonicalize.ts`) infers `schedule.kind` and `payload.kind` from whichever fields are present, so the model never has to deal with the nested union. Also
descriptions for `text` (implies `systemEvent`) and `mode` (wake only, not delivery mode)
have been tightened up.

The implementation now also normalises scalar toolsAllow / fallbacks into arrays and reconstructs job / patch from recoverable flat fields when the request is clearly a cron add/update call.  This deals with an issue found in testing where openclaw incorrectly tries toolsAllow as a scalar string, or emits a malformed non-object job / patch alongside flat fields.  

## User Impact

Upstream already recovers flat params at runtime: 
`recoverCronObjectFromFlatParams` in `cron-tool-canonicalize.ts` (with
`CRON_FLAT_PAYLOAD_KEYS` / `CRON_FLAT_SCHEDULE_KEYS`)

The patch simply exposes in the model-facing schema what the runtime already accepts but doesn't show. Note the nested `job` form still works also.  There is no negative user impact to the fix.

## Evidence

Tested on OpenClaw gateway version 2026.6.10
OS: Linux Mint 22.3 (Zena)
Kernel: Linux 6.17.0-23-generic (x86_64)
LLMs used for testing: Local Gemma 4 26b Q5 (llama.cpp); openai/gpt-5.4
Tests designed and run by: Claude (Anthropic Claude Opus 4.8); OpenAI Codex (gpt-5.4)

Focused validation on `fix/cron-tool-schema-fix` (`~/code/openclaw-main`) currently passes for the actual patch surface:

- `corepack pnpm test src/agents/tools/cron-tool.schema.test.ts src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts`
  - schema shard: `20 passed`
  - agents shard: `135 passed`

These tests cover:

- flat-field exposure in the model-facing cron schema
- canonicalization of malformed flat `toolsAllow` / `fallbacks`
- synthesis of `job` / `patch` from recoverable flat arguments
- the drift guard that ensures any advertised flat field is still recoverable by the canonicalizer

Earlier branch testing also included:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/cron-tool.schema.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts`
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`

Live installed testing on patched OpenClaw 2026.6.10 also succeeded in creating disposable cron jobs through the flat-field interface, confirming the path works in a real installed gateway and not only in unit tests.

This four-file branch is green on the patch-local validation that actually exercises the cron-tool
change. The remaining PR-guide blockers are upstream baseline failures outside this patch scope.

Current upstream-baseline validation also shows:

- latest `origin/main` still fails `corepack pnpm deps:shrinkwrap:check` with
  `npm-shrinkwrap.json is stale. Run pnpm deps:shrinkwrap:generate.`
- clean `origin/main` is also currently red in unrelated test areas, including
  `src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts` and `src/media-understanding/image.test.ts`
  (reported for completeness only)

So the branch is green for the cron-tool patch itself, while the remaining `check` / full-suite
`test` reds are upstream, pre-existing, and unrelated to this four-file change. codex review --base origin/main stated the patch appears to correctly expose the flat cron fields and normalize them before validation without introducing a concrete regression in the touched surfaces.

target.title: fix(web-fetch): extract full HTML body content
target.body:
Closes #82685.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users and agents running `web_fetch` on an HTML page could receive only the page title instead of visible body content when Readability returned non-empty title-only output.

The linked issue did not include the original URL or a full HTML fixture, so this update keeps the problem statement tied to the reported invariant: title/header-only extraction must not be treated as a successful body extraction.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime now treats title-only Readability output as incomplete after normalizing markdown/plain text, then continues through the existing recovery order: configured provider output first, local raw HTML body cleanup last. The local body cleanup path also scans for the real document body while skipping fake `<body>` tags inside comments, raw-text containers, and inert or nested `<template>` content.

This keeps the fix scoped to the `web_fetch` runtime extraction decision. It does not change shared HTML-to-markdown helpers, provider configuration, network/auth/security policy, migrations, schema, public API shape, or the provider catalog.

## User Impact

Users and agents should now get visible page body content instead of title-only output for this class of HTML extraction failure. If a configured provider can handle the page, provider output still wins before local raw HTML cleanup, preserving the existing compatibility boundary.

No config, migration, auth, secrets, network capability, or tool execution behavior changes are required.

## Evidence

- Runtime proof: ran the real Readability extractor, then ran the real `web_fetch` tool path against a deterministic HTML fixture where Readability returns only the title. External network access was not required for this proof.

  ```text
  web_fetch title-only fallback proof
  fixture url: https://fixture.openclaw.test/title-only-aside-body
  readability.title: "Sample Page"
  readability.text: "Sample Page"
  readability.titleOnly: true
  web_fetch.status: 200
  web_fetch.contentType: text/html
  web_fetch.extractor: raw-html
  web_fetch.title.hasSamplePage: true
  web_fetch.text.hasBodyMarker: true
  ```

- Focused validation: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/web-tools.fetch.test.ts` passed with 1 test file and 37 tests passing.
- Regression coverage includes title-only Readability text, markdown heading title-only output, fake body tags inside comments/raw-text/template/declaration regions, nested inert templates, and the provider-before-raw fallback order.
- Proof limitation: the exact reporter page was not available from the issue, so the runtime proof uses a deterministic representative fixture that reproduces the title-only/body-cleanup invariant.
- Current state: ready for maintainer review after the updated branch is submitted and CI reruns on the PR.

target.title: fix(thread-ownership): bound 409 response read and preserve cancel semantics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The thread-ownership plugin's 409 conflict path still used an unbounded `resp.json()`, inconsistent with the bounded readers shipped across the other channel/provider success paths (discord webhook, huggingface `/v1/models`, and others already use `readProviderJsonResponse` / `readResponseTextLimited`). A compromised or buggy forwarder returning a multi-GB 409 body would buffer the entire body before `JSON.parse` even runs, OOMing the agent.

> Scope note: an earlier version of this branch also bounded the discord webhook success read and the huggingface `/v1/models` read. Those two were superseded upstream by #98098 (`fix(providers): bound successful OAuth and webhook responses`) and #101079 (`fix(extensions/huggingface): bound model discovery JSON response read to prevent OOM`), which both use the shared `readProviderJsonResponse` helper. This branch was rebased onto current `main` and now carries only the thread-ownership fix, which is still open on `main` (unbounded `resp.json()`).

## Why This Change Was Made

Same partial-hardening pattern already shipped across comfy, anthropic-oauth, sms, matrix, telegram, and discord/api.ts. The thread-ownership 409 path was the remaining outlier: its success/409 body read was unbounded and reached `JSON.parse` over an internal forwarder whose response size is not guaranteed.

A 409 from the forwarder means another agent owns the thread — the send must be cancelled regardless of whether the body parses. The fix preserves that cancel semantics even when the body is truncated or malformed.

## User Impact

Well-formed 409 responses unchanged. A huge/non-JSON/truncated 409 body is capped (8 KiB) and the send is still cancelled (owner logged as `unknown`), instead of OOMing the agent or crashing the ownership check. The prior behavior on a truncated 409 body was an unhandled `SyntaxError` from `JSON.parse` that fell into the outer catch and allowed the send — this fix makes a malformed 409 cancel correctly.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Unbounded thread-ownership 409 body read; OOM risk + lost cancel semantics on a truncated/malformed 409.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v24.14.0, commit `47c03956dd` on branch `fix/unbounded-success-json-reads` (rebased onto current `main`).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx verify-thread-ownership-real.mjs` — stands up a REAL local HTTP server as the Slack forwarder and drives the REAL exported plugin entrypoint (`register` + the `message_sending` hook) from `extensions/thread-ownership/index.ts`. `globalThis.fetch` is NOT mocked: the production `fetchWithSsrFGuard` handles each request over a real socket (each case's local server confirms it served the 409). The SSRF guard is told to allow private-network access, exactly like prod.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (live stdout, copied verbatim — non-mocked, real forwarder + real plugin entrypoint):

  ```text
  Driving the real exported plugin entrypoint (register + message_sending hook).
  globalThis.fetch is NOT mocked; each case uses its own real local HTTP server.

  Case 1 (well-formed 409 body):
    [PASS]   local server served the 409
    [PASS]   cancel=true — result={"cancel":true}
    [PASS]   owner parsed as 'other-agent' — [info] thread-ownership: cancelled send to C100:111 — owned by other-agent

  Case 2 (malformed/truncated 409 body):
    [PASS]   local server served the 409
    [PASS]   cancel=true — result={"cancel":true}
    [PASS]   owner falls back to 'unknown' — [info] thread-ownership: cancelled send to C101:222 — owned by unknown

  Case 3 (oversized 409 body, 64 KiB vs 8 KiB cap):
    [PASS]   local server served the 409
    [PASS]   cancel=true — result={"cancel":true}
    [PASS]   owner falls back to 'unknown' (64 KiB body truncated at 8 KiB cap -> unparseable) — [info] thread-ownership: cancelled send to C102:333 — owned by unknown

  Verdict: all cases PASS — well-formed 409 cancels with parsed owner; malformed + oversized 409 still cancel (owner 'unknown') without crash or unbounded buffering.
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Against a real local forwarder, the real `message_sending` hook (driven through `register`) returns `{ cancel: true }` for all three 409 shapes. A well-formed 409 cancels with the parsed owner (`other-agent`); a malformed/truncated 409 and a 64 KiB oversized 409 both cancel with owner `unknown` — proving the body is capped (the oversized body is truncated at the 8 KiB cap, so `JSON.parse` fails and the 409 status alone drives cancellation) without unbounded buffering or a crash.
- **What was not tested:** A live multi-GB response from a production forwarder. The proof drives the real production entrypoint over a real socket; the oversized case uses a 64 KiB body (8x the cap) to exercise the truncation path deterministically.

## Tests and validation

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/thread-ownership/index.test.ts   (22 passed)
```

## Risk checklist

- Cap size: thread-ownership 8 KiB (409 owner body is ~30 bytes).
- User-visible behavior: Yes (intended) — a malformed/truncated 409 body now cancels the send (owner `unknown`) instead of throwing into the outer catch and allowing it; well-formed 409 unchanged.
- Config/env/migration: No.
- Security: Yes (improvement) — bounds the 409 body read, mitigating OOM from a compromised/buggy forwarder.
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: Yes (bounded) — touches one extension; uses the shared `readResponseTextLimited` already used elsewhere.
- Highest-risk area: a legitimate 409 body exceeding 8 KiB would fail to parse and cancel with `owner=unknown` — but a 409 owner field is tiny in practice, and the cancel behavior is the correct 409 semantics, so this is strictly safer than the prior crash/allow.
- Mitigation: existing test suite passes (22 tests) + real local-forwarder runtime verification of well-formed / malformed / oversized 409 cancel semantics.

Closes: N/A (no existing issue)

target.title: fix(secrets): skip gateway RPC for non-gateway exec SecretRefs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On every agent **reply** turn, the gateway logs a noisy UNAVAILABLE failure for `secrets.resolve` when a model-provider credential uses an **exec** SecretRef. The gateway's command-path resolution cannot execute exec providers, so the RPC always fails before falling back locally — producing ~1 log line per turn.

```
[ws] ⇄ res ✗ secrets.resolve 6ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=secrets.resolve failed
```

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing code in `resolveCommandSecretRefsViaGateway` already skips the gateway RPC when **gateway-credential** paths (`gateway.auth.*`, `gateway.remote.*`) use exec SecretRefs, because the gateway can't resolve them via the RPC. The same logic applies to model-provider/agent-runtime paths — `collectActiveGatewayExecSecretRefCredentialPaths` only looks at gateway paths, so model-provider exec refs were still triggering the futile RPC.

Fix: add a `collectConfiguredTargetExecRefPaths` helper and check for non-gateway exec SecretRefs before calling the gateway RPC. When any are found, skip the RPC and resolve locally (same pattern as the gateway-credential skip).

## Evidence

All 35 tests in `command-secret-gateway.test.ts` pass.

New test: **"skips gateway resolution when non-gateway targets use exec SecretRefs"**
- Configures a talk provider with exec-backed apiKey
- Verifies `callGateway` is never invoked
- Verifies the exec provider is executed and resolves correctly
- Verifies the diagnostic includes "skipped gateway secrets.resolve because configured secrets use exec SecretRefs"

Updated tests:
- **"keeps local exec SecretRef fallback enabled by default"** — now verifies the gateway RPC is proactively skipped rather than attempted and failed
- **"skips local exec SecretRef fallback when the caller disallows exec providers"** — same proactive skip

## Merge Risk

Low — narrow check added just before the gateway RPC call, reusing existing `collectConfiguredTargetRefPaths` data. The `resolveCommandSecretRefsWithoutGateway` path is already exercised by the gateway-credential exec skip. Non-exec ref paths are unaffected.

target.title: Harden jq safe-bin semantics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Operators can explicitly configure exec safe bins for narrow stdin-oriented tools. `jq` is broader than that model: it can read environment data and load jq code through explicit modules and startup files, which means approval-free safe-bin execution cannot be constrained to the intended stdin-only behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change makes `jq` fail closed in the safe-bin semantic gate, matching the existing treatment for other tools whose semantics cannot be validated to stdin-only. Doctor and security audit now warn about jq/risky safe-bin entries without scaffolding profiles that can never satisfy the runtime semantic gate.

Operators can still run jq through an explicit allowlist entry or the normal approval prompt.

## User Impact

`jq` commands no longer qualify for approval-free execution through `tools.exec.safeBins`, even for simple field filters. Configurations that intentionally rely on jq should use an explicit allowlist entry for the trusted jq path or allow the approval prompt. Other safe-bin tools such as `head`, `tail`, `tr`, and `wc` are unchanged.

AI-assisted: yes.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-safe-bin-semantics.test.ts src/infra/exec-safe-bin-policy.test.ts src/infra/exec-approvals-safe-bins.test.ts src/infra/exec-safe-bin-runtime-policy.test.ts src/commands/doctor/shared/exec-safe-bins.test.ts src/security/audit-exec-safe-bins.test.ts src/infra/exec-approvals-config.test.ts src/infra/exec-approvals.test.ts`

target.title: fix: emit failover event for successful model fallback chains
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `emitFailoverEvent` was only called from the cooldown/suspend path, so the OTEL `model.failover` diagnostic was never emitted when model fallback actually happened. Multi-hop chains and all-failed storms were invisible in traces.

**Solution**: Emit a `model.failover` diagnostic event at each failed-candidate → next-candidate transition so every fallback hop produces a diagnostic event with `from/to provider/model`, `reason`, and `cascadeDepth`. The existing `openclaw.failover.*` OTEL attributes already convey that a fallback occurred — no new undocumented span attributes needed.

**What changed**: `model-fallback.ts`: After recording each failed candidate, emit `model.failover` when a next candidate exists. `diagnostics-otel/service.ts`: Reverted to baseline (no undocumented `has_fallback` attribute).

**What did NOT change**: Cooldown/suspend `emitFailoverEvent` call site, fallback decision logging, session suspension, model candidate resolution.

Fixes #102015

## What Problem This Solves

Model fallback chains happen in production (rate limits, provider outages), but `model.failover` diagnostic events were only emitted when models were suspended by cooldown. Actual fallback transitions — where a candidate failed and a different model was tried next — produced zero diagnostic events. Operators could not detect multi-hop fallback cascades or retry storms.

## Root Cause

`emitFailoverEvent` was only called from the `suspend_lanes` cooldown decision path. The fallback loop (`runWithModelFallbackInternal`) never emitted diagnostics for failed-candidate → next-candidate transitions.

## Design decision (review feedback)

The emit is at the **failed-candidate → next-candidate transition** rather than at success. This covers both all-failed chains (every hop) and successful chains (the last failed hop before the winning candidate). The undocumented `has_fallback` span attribute was removed — `openclaw.failover.*` attributes are sufficient.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Each failed-candidate → next-candidate transition in the fallback loop emits a `model.failover` diagnostic event.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node 24.13.1 — real `emitFailoverEvent` + `onInternalDiagnosticEvent` API

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```terminal
npx tsx proof-script.mjs
pnpm test -- src/agents/model-fallback.test.ts src/agents/model-fallback.probe.test.ts extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```terminal_output

Proof 1: model.failover events with full fallback chain data

  minimax/m2.7 → kimi/k2.6                 reason=overloaded depth=2
  openai/gpt-5.5 → (suspend)               reason=billing

Result: ✅ PASS

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
All have reason: true
All have fromProvider: true
Transitions have toProvider: true
Transitions have cascadeDepth: true
Result: ✅ PASS

Proof 3: No undocumented has_fallback attribute
Result: ✅ PASS

✅ ALL CHECKS PASSED
```

Unit tests: 115+20+107 = 242/242 passed.

**Observed result after the fix**: Each failed-candidate → next-candidate hop emits a `model.failover` diagnostic event with `fromProvider/fromModel/toProvider/toModel/reason/cascadeDepth`. Transition events are structurally consistent with the existing suspend-path events. No undocumented attributes leak.

**What was not tested**: End-to-end OTLP exporter requiring a configured external telemetry receiver.

## Risk checklist

- [x] Low risk — only adds diagnostic event emissions at transition points, no behavioral change
- [x] All 242 existing tests pass unchanged
- [x] 2 files, net +0 lines (move from success path to transition point)
- [x] Cooldown/suspend `emitFailoverEvent` unchanged
- [x] L2 proof: real `emitFailoverEvent` + `onInternalDiagnosticEvent` API

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Matrix users could see MiniMax reasoning-only monitor replies when the reply text used MiniMax `mm:` thinking tags such as `<mm:think>`, `<mm:thinking>`, or `<mm:thought>`.

Without this patch, the Matrix monitor reply delivery path could treat those hidden reasoning blocks as ordinary visible text and send them into the Matrix room.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Matrix already suppresses reasoning-only replies before `sendMessageMatrix`; this change aligns that Matrix-local classifier with the MiniMax `mm:` thinking-tag namespace used by sibling reasoning-tag paths.
- The fix is intentionally narrow: it only expands the existing Matrix thinking-tag regex family and keeps the send pipeline, auth/config behavior, room/thread behavior, media delivery, migrations, dependencies, and public plugin API unchanged.
- A focused regression test locks in that three `mm:` reasoning-only replies are dropped while a normal visible answer in the same batch still sends.

target.title: fix #95295: [Bug]: Web UI sidebar hides existing child-spawned subagent sessions across agent scopes
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #95295

- **Problem:** Child-spawned subagent sessions created via `sessions_spawn()` exist in session stores and on disk, but do not appear in the Web UI sidebar Recent Sessions when viewed from another agent scope. Users cannot rediscover cross-agent subagent work from the sidebar.
- **Root cause:** When the sidebar requests Recent Sessions it sends `agentId`, which scopes both layers — the backend `loadCombinedSessionStoreForGateway(cfg, { agentId })` loads only that agent's store, and the frontend `getVisibleSessionRows()` filters out `isSubagentSessionKey` / `spawnedBy` rows. Cross-agent child sessions are dropped before they reach the UI.

## Solution

Re-implemented on top of the current Control UI architecture (the prior approach targeted `session-picker.ts`, which main removed in #100648 when it moved to palette-only search and grouped sessions).

- **Default-off sidebar "All agents" toggle** in the Recent Sessions header (next to the agent-scope selector). It is the only entry point; all other callers (CLI `sessions.list`, command palette, chat) keep their existing scoped behavior unchanged.
- When toggled on, the sidebar refresh sends **no `agentId`**. The backend already supports this: with no `agentId`, `loadCombinedSessionStoreForGateway` runs `resolveAllAgentSessionStoreTargetsSync` (all agent stores) and `filterSessionEntries` keeps every entry including cross-agent children — so no backend/protocol change is needed.
- `getVisibleSessionRows` gains an `includeChildSessions` option, gated by a new `recentSessionsAllAgents` field on `SessionNavigationInput`. Default (off) preserves the existing scoped filter exactly.

## What changed

- `ui/src/lib/sessions/navigation.ts` — add `recentSessionsAllAgents` to `SessionNavigationInput` and `includeChildSessions` to `getVisibleSessionRows`; in All-agents mode, stop dropping `isSubagentSessionKey`/`spawnedBy` rows and skip the active-agent filter.
- `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts` — add `recentSessionsAllAgents` state, a `toggleRecentSessionsAgentScope` handler that refreshes without `agentId` (and restores the scoped `agentId` when toggled off), the toggle button in the ungrouped-session header, and the `recentSessionsAllAgents` input to `resolveSessionNavigation`.
- `ui/src/styles/layout.css` — styles for the `.sidebar-recent-sessions__scope` toggle button, matching the existing `.sidebar-agent-scope` pill.
- `ui/src/lib/sessions/navigation.test.ts` — two regression tests: child-spawned sessions stay hidden by default; they appear (with the agent filter unscoped) only in All-agents mode.

## What was not tested or remains unavailable

- **No redacted live Control UI screenshot/recording.** This environment (Windows, no running OpenClaw gateway with a multi-agent `sessions_spawn()` setup) cannot produce the live sidebar proof ClawSweeper requested. Verification is limited to unit tests + typecheck + lint below. A maintainer or contributor with a multi-agent Control UI setup should confirm scoped vs. All-agents visibility on persisted child sessions.
- Backend behavior (all-agent store load on omitted `agentId`) is read from source (`src/config/sessions/combined-store-gateway.ts`, `src/gateway/session-utils.ts` `filterSessionEntries`) and covered by the existing frontend contract, not re-exercised end-to-end here.

## Verification

- `vitest run src/lib/sessions/` — 40/40 passed (6 files), including 2 new All-agents cases in `navigation.test.ts`.
- `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` (covers `ui/**`) — 0 errors in changed files. (1 pre-existing, unrelated error in `packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts`: missing `markdown-it-cjk-friendly` module, present on clean main.)
- `oxlint` on the three changed `.ts` files — 0 warnings, 0 errors.

## Risk

- **Product boundary:** the toggle is sidebar-only and default-off, so chat/checkpoint/CLI `sessions.list` behavior is unchanged. The All-agents refresh is a separate, user-initiated request and does not alter the shared session capability's default scoped refreshes.
- **Performance:** an All-agents refresh loads every agent store; for deployments with very many agents/sessions this is heavier than a scoped request, but it only happens on explicit toggle and reverts to scoped on the next toggle off.
