target.title: improve(ui): bring back openclaw brand, remove desktop topbar + breadcrumbs
target.body:
brand is important 🤓

## What Problem This Solves

The desktop chat topbar was carrying controls that did not need to live there. The breadcrumb was not useful, and Search plus the sidebar toggle fit better in the existing sidebar pattern.

This PR brings the OpenClaw brand back to the sidebar, places Search and the sidebar toggle next to it, adds Cmd+B to open and close the sidebar, and keeps the mobile topbar with centered OpenClaw branding plus a Search icon.

It also folds in the remaining sidebar polish from #100963 and #100918: compact sidebar timestamps, scoped visual session highlighting, a single-icon color-mode toggle, sidebar sorting popover placement, compact rail search, and collapsed-rail active-state cleanup.

## Screenshots

Mobile topbar in this PR:

![Mobile topbar in this PR](https://lunar-bugle-xt6w.here.now/pr-101017-mobile-app-shell-header-controls.png)

Desktop sidebar and chat shell in this PR:

![Desktop sidebar and chat shell in this PR](https://lunar-bugle-xt6w.here.now/pr-101017-desktop-app-shell-header-controls.png)

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps desktop navigation controls in the sidebar, where the app already has a calm and consistent pattern for global navigation. The terminal action moves to the chat workspace rail, so it stays available without bringing back the desktop topbar.

Mobile keeps the topbar because that is still the right place for drawer navigation and Search on small screens. It now shows the OpenClaw brand in the center and relegates Search to an icon on the right.

## User Impact

Desktop users get the brand back in the sidebar, fewer controls in the chat header area, and a keyboard shortcut for opening and closing the sidebar. Sidebar session rows keep the previous focus behavior for keyboard access, while the selected-session highlight is scoped to Chat. The color-mode control is a single footer icon that cycles modes on click.

Mobile users get a branded topbar with navigation on the left and Search on the right.

- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check ui/src/app/app-host.ts ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts ui/src/components/app-topbar.ts ui/src/components/theme-mode-toggle.ts ui/src/components/terminal/terminal-panel.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-state.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-session-workspace.ts ui/src/e2e/sidebar-customization.e2e.test.ts ui/src/styles/layout.css ui/src/styles/layout.mobile.css ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts`

target.title: fix(diagnostics-otel): set CLIENT span kind on model call and tool execution spans
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

All OpenClaw trace spans use `SpanKind.INTERNAL` by default, making external API calls (LLM providers, tool executions) invisible as distinct dependency nodes in distributed tracing tools. Model call spans (model.call.*) only got `CLIENT` kind when the `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental` opt-in was set; tool execution spans (tool.execution.*) never carried an explicit kind at all.

- Problem: Trace visualization tools (Jaeger, Zipkin) show all spans as flat internal operations — no way to distinguish network latency from processing time
- Solution: Set `SpanKind.CLIENT` unconditionally on model call spans and on actual tool execution spans (started/completed/error). Blocked tool spans (policy-denied, no outgoing request) keep the implicit `INTERNAL` default.
- What changed: `extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.ts` (modelCallSpanKind + 3 actual tool span sites; blocked path unchanged), `service.test.ts` (updated assertions + blocked span test), `docs/gateway/opentelemetry.md` (docs reflect kind is no longer gated)
- What did NOT change: GenAI semconv span naming/attributes remain gated behind `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN`; model.failover, context.assembled, and other internal-only spans keep their existing kind behavior

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #102017
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

The OpenTelemetry SpanKind specification defines `CLIENT` for outgoing requests to external services. LLM API calls (OpenAI, xAI, Ollama, etc.) and tool executions (shell commands, HTTP requests, filesystem operations) semantically represent client requests. Using `INTERNAL` for these spans breaks distributed tracing — latency analysis cannot distinguish network round-trips from internal processing, and dependency graphs in Jaeger/Zipkin cannot show external service dependencies.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Model call and tool execution spans now carry `SpanKind.CLIENT` (value 2) instead of the default `SpanKind.INTERNAL`
- Real environment tested: Linux Node 24, branch `fix/otel-span-kind-client-102017`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
# Run the full test suite
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.9

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  108 passed (108)

# Source-level verification:

# modelCallSpanKind() now unconditionally returns CLIENT:
$ grep -A 3 "function modelCallSpanKind" extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.ts
function modelCallSpanKind(): SpanKind {
  return SpanKind.CLIENT;
}

# 3 actual tool.execution span creation points carry kind=CLIENT:
$ grep -B 1 "kind: SpanKind.CLIENT" extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.ts
            kind: SpanKind.CLIENT,    # tool.execution.started
            kind: SpanKind.CLIENT,    # tool.execution.completed
            kind: SpanKind.CLIENT,    # tool.execution.error

# Blocked tool span has no explicit kind (INTERNAL default):
$ grep -A 5 "outcome.*blocked" extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.ts | grep -c "kind"
0

# Assertions verifying the span kind values:
$ grep -B 1 "kind).toBe" extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts
expect(modelOptions?.kind).toBe(2);                  # model call span
expect(toolOptions?.kind).toBe(2);                   # tool execution span
expect(Object.hasOwn(blockedOptions ?? {}, "kind")).toBe(false);  # blocked span
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. Model call spans (model.call.submitted/completed/error) always export with `SpanKind.CLIENT` — no longer gated behind `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN`
  2. Actual tool execution spans (tool.execution.started/completed/error) always export with `SpanKind.CLIENT`
  3. Blocked tool spans (policy-denied, no outgoing request) keep `SpanKind.INTERNAL` — semantically correct
  4. GenAI semconv env var continues to control span naming (openclaw.model.call vs gen_ai.*) independently
  5. Internal-only spans (model.failover, context.assembled, memory.pressure, session.stuck) remain `SpanKind.INTERNAL`
- What was not tested: Live Jaeger/Zipkin collector ingestion (requires external infrastructure).
- Real OTel exporter proof via `ConsoleSpanExporter` (production OTel SDK, not mocked):

```console
--- Span 1: openclaw.model.call ---
kind: 2 (SpanKind.CLIENT)  ← PR sets this unconditionally

--- Span 2: openclaw.tool.execution ---
kind: 2 (SpanKind.CLIENT)  ← PR sets this on actual exec spans

--- Span 3: openclaw.tool.execution (blocked) ---
kind: 0 (SpanKind.INTERNAL) ← PR keeps default, no explicit kind set
```

The exported JSON from real `@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-node` + `ConsoleSpanExporter` confirms:
- `openclaw.model.call` → **kind=2 (CLIENT)** — correct for LLM API calls
- `openclaw.tool.execution` (actual) → **kind=2 (CLIENT)** — correct for outgoing tool requests
- `openclaw.tool.execution` (blocked) → **kind=0 (INTERNAL)** — correct, no HTTP request was made

```json
{"name":"openclaw.model.call","kind":2,"attributes":{"gen_ai.operation.name":"chat","gen_ai.request.model":"gpt-5.5"}}
{"name":"openclaw.tool.execution","kind":2,"attributes":{"tool.name":"browser","tool.source":"mcp"}}
{"name":"openclaw.tool.execution","kind":0,"attributes":{"tool.name":"browser","tool.source":"mcp","openclaw.tool.blocked":"true"}}
```

## Root Cause (if applicable)

PR #86191 (`f824e1596ad`) introduced `modelCallSpanKind()` which only returned `SpanKind.CLIENT` when `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental` was set, otherwise `undefined` → `INTERNAL`. Tool execution spans were added without any kind override since their introduction.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

The test suite (`service.test.ts`) has four assertions specific to span kind:
- Default model call: `expect(modelOptions?.kind).toBe(2)` (was `toBe(false)` for absent kind)
- Tool execution (error path): `expect(toolOptions?.kind).toBe(2)` (new)
- Tool execution (content capture): `expect(toolOptions?.kind).toBe(2)` (new)
- Blocked tool span: `expect(Object.hasOwn(blockedOptions ?? {}, "kind")).toBe(false)` (new, focused test)

108 tests pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None directly visible to end users. Trace data consumers (Jaeger, Zipkin, Grafana Tempo, Datadog) will see `kind=CLIENT` on model call and tool execution spans, enabling proper dependency graphs and latency breakdown.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Source-level verification of all relevant span creation points; test assertion updates checked for correctness
- Edge cases checked: GenAI semconv opt-in still controls span names/attributes independently; tool spans that go through the trusted span tracking path (takeTrackedTrustedSpan) inherit the same kind from the original span
- What you did NOT verify: Live Jaeger collector round-trip; non-Node runtimes

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — span kind change only affects how trace backends classify spans, not runtime behavior
- [x] Config/env changes? Only the documentation of `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN` — no actual config surface changed
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. Unconditional CLIENT for model calls + CLIENT for actual tool executions, blocked tool spans kept INTERNAL. No new config or env var needed.
- **Refactor needed**: No. The changes are self-contained in 5 locations within one file.
- **Alternative considered**: Keeping the GenAI-semconv gate but changing span kind to always be CLIENT regardless of naming — this is what we implemented. Another option was adding a new config knob for span kind per span type, which would be over-engineered for this use case.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: None significant. SpanKind is a classification tag on exported spans — changing from INTERNAL to CLIENT affects trace visualization only, not runtime behavior, data paths, or permission checks.
- **Mitigation**: All existing span names, attributes, and lifecycle are preserved. The change is opt-in only at the trace-consumer level (users who export traces to Jaeger/Zipkin will see the improvement).
- **Compatibility**: Users currently ingesting OpenClaw traces who have built dashboards/filters based on `kind=INTERNAL` will need to update those filters. No users have reported relying on the INTERNAL kind value.

Fixes #102017

target.title: fix(doctor): keep scrubbed error truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

- Reuse the shared UTF-16 safe truncation helper when doctor scrubs long error messages.
- Add a regression test through the doctor lint thrown-check path so emoji/surrogate boundaries stay valid.
- Keep the existing 256-character cap, control-character stripping, and `...` suffix behavior.

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor lint/repair flows sanitize thrown health-check errors before showing them in terminal diagnostics. The sanitizer removed control characters correctly, but its length cap used `slice(0, ERR_MESSAGE_MAX_LEN - 3)`. When a long error message placed an emoji exactly on that boundary, the slice kept only the high surrogate before appending `...`, leaving invalid UTF-16 in the doctor output.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Users running doctor commands can see long health-check error messages in terminal output. With the old truncation, a message containing emoji or another surrogate-pair character at the cap boundary could print a replacement glyph or otherwise carry malformed UTF-16. After this change, doctor keeps the same bounded output shape while dropping incomplete surrogate pairs.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High — the diff is limited to the shared doctor error-message scrubber and one focused regression test, with fresh local runtime proof on the exact doctor lint path.

## Origin / follow-up

Follows #101600.

- **Gap this fills:** #101600 covered the same UTF-16 truncation class in terminal output, but `src/flows/doctor-error-message.ts` still used a raw UTF-16 `slice` for scrubbed doctor error messages.
- **Consistency:** This patch uses the existing `truncateUtf16Safe` helper instead of introducing a doctor-specific truncation path.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

No linked issue anchor for this follow-up. I checked open PRs for the same target and wording:

- `scrubDoctorErrorMessage`
- `doctor UTF-16 truncation`
- `doctor error message truncation`

- **Related open PR scan:** All three exact open PR searches returned `[]` in `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-followup-101600-evidence/open-pr-competition-exact.json`.
- **What did NOT change:** No unrelated truncation helpers, doctor check selection, repair behavior, config schema, provider routing, or channel delivery behavior changed; this PR only covers doctor lint/repair error-message truncation through `scrubDoctorErrorMessage`.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `scrubDoctorErrorMessage` is the source-of-truth boundary for doctor error text because both lint and repair flows call it before surfacing thrown health-check errors; no public config/schema contract, default, migration, or partial override behavior is involved.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Long doctor health-check error messages containing a surrogate-pair character at the truncation boundary no longer produce an unpaired surrogate in the user-visible doctor finding message.
- **Canonical reachability path:** A shipped health check can throw an `Error` during doctor lint/repair execution → `runDoctorLintChecks` / repair catch blocks call `scrubDoctorErrorMessage(err)` → doctor returns a finding/warning message shown in terminal output. No user config/schema path is involved because the input is a runtime `Error.message` from the health-check execution boundary.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; the proof runs the actual `runDoctorLintChecks` production path with a health check that throws the boundary-case error.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`; provider documented range/constraint is N/A because this is local doctor terminal formatting, not provider config.
- **Real environment tested:** Local Linux OpenClaw worktree at `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/followup-101600` with installed workspace dependencies.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
source /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-followup-101600-evidence/context.env
cd "$TASK_WORKTREE"
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/flows/doctor-lint-flow.test.ts src/flows/doctor-repair-flow.test.ts
pnpm exec tsx -e '<script importing runDoctorLintChecks and throwing A*252 + emoji + B*10 from a health check>'
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  18 passed (18)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 12.81s
```

```json
{
  "checkId": "emoji-boom",
  "severity": "error",
  "startsWithDoctorPrefix": true,
  "endsWithEllipsis": true,
  "hasUnpairedSurrogate": false,
  "findingMessageLength": 275,
  "messageTail": "AAAAAAAAAAAAA..."
}
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The doctor lint finding still has the expected `health check threw:` prefix and `...` suffix, and `hasUnpairedSurrogate` is `false` for the boundary-case thrown error.
- **What was not tested:** No third-party provider/channel/Desktop/Mantis path was tested; this behavior is local doctor runtime formatting with no external service boundary.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

## Review findings addressed

N/A — new follow-up PR; no reviewer findings yet.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/flows/doctor-lint-flow.test.ts`
- **Scenario locked in:** A regression test health check throws an `Error` whose message is `A.repeat(252) + emoji + B.repeat(10)`, placing the emoji surrogate pair exactly on the scrubber truncation boundary.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The test goes through `runDoctorLintChecks` instead of calling only the helper, so it protects the user-visible doctor finding path that prepends `health check threw:` after scrubbing without adding broader fixtures or mocks.
- Added `runDoctorLintChecks` regression coverage for a thrown error whose emoji lands on the scrubber truncation boundary.
- Verified the new test failed before the production fix with `expected true to be false` for `hasUnpairedSurrogate(message)`.
- Verified after the fix with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/flows/doctor-lint-flow.test.ts src/flows/doctor-repair-flow.test.ts`.

## Patch quality notes

- **Patch quality notes:** The production change is a one-line replacement of raw `slice` with the existing shared UTF-16 safe truncation helper. The test helper's boolean returns are only local assertion logic for detecting unpaired surrogate halves; they do not add production fallback/default behavior.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk: message-delivery` was considered because this file formats messages shown by doctor, but it does not route or deliver channel messages.
- **Risk explanation:** The changed behavior is limited to the final truncation boundary for over-limit doctor error text. It does not alter check execution, findings, repair logic, channel delivery, or provider behavior.
- **Why acceptable:** The cap, control-character stripping, and ellipsis suffix remain intact. At the exact surrogate boundary, the scrubber may keep one fewer UTF-16 code unit so the output stays valid rather than returning a dangling surrogate.

## What was not changed

- No doctor check selection, severity, or repair behavior changed.
- No provider/channel behavior changed.
- No config schema, defaults, migrations, or public API changed.
- No lockfile or dependency changes were made.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The source of the bug is `scrubDoctorErrorMessage` using raw `String.prototype.slice` for the doctor error-message contract; that caused a UTF-16 surrogate pair to be cut between its high and low halves before appending `...`.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The scrubber is the shared source-of-truth for doctor lint/repair error messages. Replacing the raw slice there with the existing UTF-16 safe truncation helper fixes every doctor caller that routes thrown errors through this sanitizer without adding downstream fallbacks or caller-specific workarounds.

target.title: fix(gateway): pass authProfileStore through loopback MCP bridge for OAuth-only plugin tools

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #101967 — the CLI-backend loopback MCP path does not pass `authProfileStore`
to gateway tool resolution, so OAuth-only plugin tools (e.g. xAI `x_search`,
`code_execution`) cannot resolve auth and are silently absent from CLI sessions.

On current `main`:
- `resolveGatewayScopedTools` → `createOpenClawTools` already accepts `authProfileStore`
- But neither the prepare-time path (`prepare.ts`) nor the runtime MCP HTTP path
  (`mcp-http.ts`) provides it

## Root Cause / Fix

Add `authProfileStore?: AuthProfileStore` to `McpLoopbackScopeParams` and thread
it through the full call chain:

```
prepare.ts → ensureMcpLoopbackServer → startMcpLoopbackServer → toolCache.resolve()
                                                              → resolveMcpLoopbackScopedTools
                                                                 → resolveGatewayScopedTools
                                                                    → createOpenClawTools(authProfileStore)
```

Both the prepare-time prompt-tools path and the runtime MCP `tools/list` +
`tools/call` path now receive the auth store.

## Evidence

### Real Behavior Proof

`startMcpLoopbackServer` started with an xAI OAuth profile in the auth store.
`tools/list` queried via MCP JSON-RPC over HTTP:

```

```

The `authProfileStore` threads through the full runtime path and

visible.

Closes #101967

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running CLI-backend sessions (e.g., `claude-cli`) with OAuth-only xAI auth would never see the `x_search` and `code_execution` tools on the session tool surface. Because subagents inherit the parent session's tool list, the tools were also stripped from native-runtime Grok subagents spawned from a claude-cli main session.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway loopback MCP bridge that feeds CLI-backend sessions resolved plugin tools without passing an `authProfileStore`. Native embedded runs already passed the store, which let the xAI plugin register search/code-execution tools when an OAuth profile was present. This change threads the auth profile store through the same path:

- `resolveGatewayScopedTools` now accepts and forwards `authProfileStore` to `createOpenClawTools`.
- `resolveMcpLoopbackScopedTools` / `McpLoopbackToolCache` accept `authProfileStore`.
- `cli-runner/prepare.ts` forwards its already-loaded `authStore` when computing prompt tools.
- The MCP loopback HTTP server loads the per-session auth profile store and passes it into tool resolution.

## User Impact

CLI-backend sessions with OAuth-only xAI auth now correctly surface `x_search` and `code_execution`, and subagents spawned from those sessions inherit the tools as expected.

## Evidence

target.title: fix: clear session suspension timers on gateway shutdown
target.body:
Closes #101720

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where sessions suspended for quota or circuit reasons could leave lane auto-resume timers pending while the gateway was shutting down. Those timers could later call back into command lane concurrency after shutdown had already begun.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session-suspension module now owns a cleanup hook for pending lane auto-resume timers, and the gateway shutdown path invokes it after drain handling and before tearing down runtimes and background services. The change keeps normal TTL auto-resume behavior intact while preventing stale shutdown-time timer callbacks.

## User Impact

Gateway shutdown and restart are less likely to race with delayed session-suspension timers. Suspended lanes still auto-resume normally during regular runtime operation.

## Data Model / Upgrade Compatibility

No persisted schema or migration behavior changes. The production change only clears the in-memory `laneResumeTimers` map during gateway shutdown. Existing `quotaSuspension` entries remain schemaVersion 1 and are neither rewritten nor migrated by the new cleanup hook. The serialized-state surface ClawSweeper detected is test coverage around the existing session suspension shape, not a new stored field.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed, 2 Vitest shards.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 CI=1 PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed locally in child mode. Testbox delegation was blocked because the local Crabbox binary is 0.15.0 and the Testbox flow requires >=0.22.0; the local run also emitted Node 22.18.0 engine warnings.

## Real Behavior Proof

Ran a standalone Node/tsx proof that imports the real `suspendSession()`, real command queue state, real timers, and the real `createGatewayCloseHandler()` shutdown path. The control leg proves the pending auto-resume timer normally fires after TTL; the shutdown leg proves gateway close clears the pending timer so it cannot restore lane concurrency after teardown begins.

```text
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <standalone #101720 shutdown proof>
OpenClaw #101720 runtime proof root: /var/folders/sx/2qmmyr8s7rz8m6d22p3htynw0000gn/T/openclaw-101720-proof-pZFur4
Using real suspendSession(), real timers, real command queue, and createGatewayCloseHandler().
control after suspend: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
[session-suspension] auto-resumed lane after suspension TTL
control after ttl without shutdown: lane=main maxConcurrent=4 queued=0 active=0
shutdown case after suspend: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
[shutdown] started: proof shutdown for #101720
shutdown drainActiveSessionsForShutdown reason=shutdown
[gmail-watcher] gmail watcher stopped
[shutdown] completed cleanly in 29ms
gateway close completed warnings=[] durationMs=29
shutdown case immediately after close: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
shutdown case after ttl post-close: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
```

The important behavior is the final line: after waiting longer than the suspension TTL after gateway close, the main lane remains suspended at `maxConcurrent=0`; in the control leg, the same TTL restores the lane to `maxConcurrent=4`.

target.title: [codex] fix gateway restart-required reload drift
target.body:
## Summary

Read-only runtime-config drift diagnostics for gateway health. `openclaw health` (JSON and text) now reports when the running gateway's live config has drifted from the disk file on restart-required paths (model/provider/auth), so an operator can see that a disk-side repair or rotation is waiting on a restart instead of trusting a green health snapshot.

- Adds a `runtimeConfig` block to the health summary: `state: "ok" | "drift" | "unknown"`, live/disk `agents.defaults.model` labels, and the list of drifted paths (tracked: `agents.defaults.model`, `agents.defaults.models`, `agents.list`, `models`, `gateway.auth`, `auth.profiles`, `auth.order`, `secrets.providers`).
- Distinguishes unreadable/missing/invalid disk config (`state: "unknown"` with a generic message for non-admin callers) from real drift, and renders both drift and unknown states in text output.
- Gates config fingerprints (`liveSourceFingerprint`, `diskSourceFingerprint`) and the detailed disk-read error (which can contain the local config path or a parse-error excerpt) to admin-scoped (`operator.admin`) callers.
- Recomputes the drift summary on gateway health cache hits inside `mergeCachedHealthRuntimeState`, mirroring the existing delivery-queue / hot-reload-status recompute pattern, so read-scoped callers always see fresh drift state.

This PR is observability only. The hot-mode restart-required reload behavior change (honoring the restart plan instead of warn-and-keep) is intentionally NOT in this diff; it lives in the companion PR #89517 so behavior and diagnostics can be reviewed and landed independently. An earlier revision of this PR carried both concerns; they were split on 2026-06-08.

## What Problem This Solves

When `gateway.reload.mode` is `hot`, restart-required config changes (model/provider/auth) are warn-and-keep: the gateway logs `config reload requires gateway restart; hot mode ignoring (...)` and keeps running on the old pinned runtime config. Nothing user-visible reported that state afterwards: `openclaw health` said everything was ok while the gateway served stale model routing or an old `gateway.auth` token that no longer matched disk. Operators debugging "my config change did nothing" had only a single gateway log line to find.

This revision also resolves the outstanding ClawSweeper P1 on this PR: `openclaw health` connects least-privilege at `operator.read` and is served from the non-sensitive 60s health cache, so a cached "ok" could mask drift that appeared right after the cache was filled. The previous head gated a cache bypass on `operator.admin`, which never fired for the read-scoped CLI. Instead of extending the bypass, the drift summary is now recomputed on every cache hit (scope-aware; fingerprints stay admin-only) and the admin bypass was deleted -- no cache bypass remains.

## Evidence

All commands below were run at head `4229b9999d` (this branch rebased onto `upstream/main` at `22376d80e1`) in a worktree on macOS (darwin 25.5.0), Node 24.

Unit/regression tests:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/health.snapshot.test.ts src/commands/health.test.ts
  -> Test Files 2 passed (2), Tests 49 passed (49)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts
  -> Test Files 5 passed (5), Tests 525 passed (525)
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json                      -> clean
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json   -> clean
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <7 changed files>                        -> clean
oxfmt --check <7 changed files>                                      -> clean
```

New tests in this revision (`src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts`):

- `recomputes runtime-config drift on cache hits so read-scoped callers see fresh drift` -- cached "ok" + drift recompute -> `operator.read` cache hit (`{ cached: true }` respond flag asserted) returns `state: "drift"` with no fingerprints.
- `threads the admin scope into the cache-hit drift recompute so fingerprints stay admin-only` -- same cache-hit path with `operator.admin` receives fingerprints; background refresh still runs.
- `drops a stale cached runtime-config summary when the recompute returns none`.

Live behavior proof (redacted, exact head): see the `Real behavior proof` section below -- a sandbox gateway built from this head shows the ok -> drift transition on the plain, non-verbose, read-scoped `openclaw health` path after an external `gateway.auth.token` rotation under `mode: "hot"`.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: plain `openclaw health` (least-privilege `operator.read`, both JSON and text) reports `runtimeConfig.state: "drift"` with `driftPaths: ["gateway.auth"]` after an external `gateway.auth.token` rotation under `gateway.reload.mode: "hot"`, including when the response is served from the 60s health cache; fingerprints are omitted for read-scoped callers.

Real environment tested: sandbox gateway on macOS (darwin 25.5.0), dist built from this branch at head `4229b9999d` content, launched with `node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway --port 28934`, isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, config: `gateway.mode: "local"`, `gateway.auth: { mode: "token", token: "sandbox-token-OLD" }`, `gateway.reload: { mode: "hot", debounceMs: 100 }`, `agents.defaults.model: "openai/gpt-5.5"`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
node dist/index.js health --json                 # call 1, fills the health cache
sed -i.bak 's/sandbox-token-OLD/sandbox-token-NEW/' $SANDBOX/openclaw.json
sleep 4
```

target.title: feat(agents): add multi-pass context compaction with progress tracking
target.body:
Replace the single-pass compaction system with a multi-pass iterative
approach that continues compressing until the token budget is met or
progress stalls below a configurable threshold. This addresses persistent
issues where single-pass compaction either fails to reduce context enough
(leaving the agent over budget) or destroys too much context in one shot.

The implementation adds:

Core compaction engine:
- CompactionProgressTracker (packages/agent-core) that monitors per-pass
  token savings and halts when improvement drops below 5% or after a
  maximum number of passes (default 5)
- Multi-pass loop in compaction.ts with head/tail message protection:
  first N and last N non-system messages are preserved across passes to
  prevent amnesia on recent context and loss of initial instructions
- Structured summary prefix injected into compacted output so the LLM
  does not resume stale tasks after compaction
- CutPointResult type for tracking where each pass splits the message
  history

Pre-compaction pruning:
- Pre-compaction tool result pruning pass (src/agents/agent-hooks/
  pre-compaction-pruning.ts) that strips large tool outputs from older
  messages before the LLM summarization pass, recovering token budget
  without losing the tool call structure
- Configurable maximum age and size thresholds for pruning decisions
- Compaction safeguard hook integration point

Multi-pass orchestrator:
- src/agents/multi-pass-compaction.ts coordinates the full cycle: prune
  tool results, run compaction passes, track progress, apply summary
  prefix, and return the compacted message array with metrics
- Respects existing compaction timeout by distributing wall-clock budget
  across passes

Configuration:
- New compaction section in agents.defaults with maxPasses,
  progressThreshold, headProtectedMessages, tailProtectedMessages,
  enableToolResultPruning, and summaryPrefix fields
- Zod schema validation for all new config fields
- Sensible defaults that match current behavior when unconfigured
  (single-pass equivalent with maxPasses=1)

Test coverage (122 tests across 5 files):
- compaction-progress.test.ts: progress tracker state machine and
  threshold detection
- compaction-summary-prefix.test.ts: prefix injection and idempotency
- pre-compaction-pruning.test.ts: tool result stripping with age/size
  thresholds and message structure preservation
- multi-pass-compaction.test.ts: full orchestration loop, early exit,
  head/tail protection, timeout distribution
- config.multi-pass-compaction.test.ts: schema validation and defaults

Addresses: #37057, #2254, #5771, #64250, #60213, #92043, #77780, #58398

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw has no explicit iteration budget for agent runs. The agent loop runs until the LLM stops calling tools or a timeout fires. Existing loop detection is heuristic (content-hash dedup) which fails when volatile messageIds defeat all detection paths. This causes runaway tool-calling loops, OOM kills, and unbounded API costs.

target.title: fix: gate Gateway message action requester provenance [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where a write-scoped Gateway client could provide requester identity fields on `message.action` requests and have that identity treated as trusted channel provenance by downstream message actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway now treats requester account and sender provenance like other trusted channel-action context: only full-scope callers can bridge server-injected requester identity through the public RPC boundary. Write-scoped clients can still invoke supported message actions, but their caller-supplied requester identity and owner bit are stripped before channel dispatch.

## User Impact

Operators keep the existing `message.action` workflow for normal write-scoped clients, while channel actions that depend on trusted sender identity no longer accept spoofed requester provenance from those clients. This narrows the authorization boundary without changing channel configuration, storage, migrations, or plugin manifests.

## Evidence

- AI-assisted PR.

target.title: fix(mattermost): cap opaque, outbound, and monitor resource caches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unbounded in-process Maps across three Mattermost runtime surfaces:

| Surface | Maps | Pre-fix behavior |
|---------|------|------------------|
| **Monitor** (`monitor-resources.ts`) | per-monitor `channelCache`, `userCache` | TTL-based reuse but **no size cap** |
| **Outbound send** (`send.ts`) | `botUserCache`, `userByNameCache`, `channelByNameCache`, `dmChannelCache` | Grew with every distinct `(baseUrl, token, target)` triple |
| **Opaque target resolution** (`target-resolution.ts`) | `mattermostOpaqueTargetCache` | 26-char ID lookups cached forever |

**Concrete example:** A busy Mattermost gateway monitoring 2 000 channels and resolving 3 000 opaque user IDs retains thousands of monitor + opaque cache entries indefinitely, plus unbounded outbound resolution caches under multi-recipient routing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Centralizes cache writes through helpers that call `pruneMapToMaxSize` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime` immediately after each `.set`:

| Cache | Cap | File |
|-------|-----|------|
| Monitor `channelCache` | **1000** | `monitor-resources.ts` |
| Monitor `userCache` | **1000** | `monitor-resources.ts` |
| Outbound `botUserCache` | **256** | `send.ts` via `cacheOutboundEntry` |
| Outbound `userByNameCache` | **1024** | `send.ts` |
| Outbound `channelByNameCache` | **1024** | `send.ts` |
| Outbound `dmChannelCache` | **1024** | `send.ts` |
| Opaque `mattermostOpaqueTargetCache` | **1024** | `target-resolution.ts` |

TTL semantics for monitor caches are unchanged; eviction only bounds maximum retained entries.

## User Impact

**Before:** Mattermost-connected gateways accumulate unbounded in-process cache memory on long uptimes.

**After:** Each cache is capped; oldest insertion-order entries evict once limits are exceeded. Evicted entries behave like a cache miss (re-fetch / re-resolve on next use).

target.title: fix(acp): guard child process pipe stream errors in createAcpClient
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`createAcpClient` spawns an ACP server with `stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "inherit"]` but registered no `error` listeners on the child stdout, stdin, or process. An EPIPE or stream error on either pipe would trigger an unhandled `error` event, crashing the host Node process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added three `on("error")` handlers in `createAcpClient`:
- `agent.stdout.on("error", …)` — stdout read pipe
- `agent.stdin.on("error", …)` — stdin write pipe
- `agent.on("error", …)` — spawn-level failures

Same pattern as grep.ts (#101014), find.ts, bash tool, ssh sandbox. Exported `createAcpClient` via a `testing` namespace (#101749 conventions) so production-path tests can exercise the handlers.

## User Impact

No behavioral change for normal ACP sessions. Stream errors now log to stderr (in verbose mode) instead of crashing the gateway.

## Evidence

### Real process proof — spawned child processes, triggered EPIPE, host survived

```
$ node outputs/issue-102047/live-acp-proof.mjs

Test 1: Kill child → EPIPE on pipe (WITH handler, matches client.ts:155-159)
  Process survived — no crash. ✓

Test 2: Simultaneous stdout+stdin EPIPE → both caught
  [stdout] stdout EPIPE
  [stdin] stdin EPIPE
  Both caught (2), process survived. ✓

Test 3: Process-level error (ENOENT) → caught, no crash
  [process] spawn /nonexistent/binary ENOENT
  ENOENT caught: true, host survived. ✓

All 3 live tests passed
```

Without the error handlers from this PR, each test would crash the Node process with `Unhandled 'error' event`.

### Production-path tests — calls createAcpClient, emits errors on its pipes

```
 ✓ registers error handler on stdout through createAcpClient
 ✓ registers error handler on stdin through createAcpClient
 ✓ registers error handler on child process through createAcpClient
 ✓ handles simultaneous stdout+stdin errors through createAcpClient
 ✓ negative control: PassThrough without error listener throws

```

### Production handler locations

```
src/acp/client.ts:157:  agent.stdout.on("error", (err) => onStreamError("stdout", err));
src/acp/client.ts:158:  agent.stdin.on("error", (err) => onStreamError("stdin", err));
```

target.title: fix(agents): keep extension exec truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

- Keep extension/custom-tool `exec` retained stdout and stderr UTF-16 safe when output is caller-capped.
- Reuse the shared `sliceUtf16Safe` helper for both tail-retention and default output-limit truncation.
- Add regression coverage for caller-supplied caps and the default output-limit path.

## What Problem This Solves

Extension runtime commands can return stdout/stderr containing non-BMP characters such as emoji. `execCommand` retained output with `String.prototype.slice`, so a cap that landed between UTF-16 surrogate halves could return a dangling surrogate in the retained stream.

The anchor PR fixed the same class of truncation bug for exec auto-reviewer rationale text. This follow-up applies the same shared UTF-16-safe truncation invariant to extension/custom-tool command output retention.

## User Impact

Users running extensions or custom tools that emit emoji or other non-BMP text could receive broken retained stdout/stderr after truncation. That broken text can be surfaced as command output, diagnostics, or model-visible tool output. After this patch, truncation may retain one fewer UTF-16 code unit at a split boundary, but it will not return an invalid surrogate half.

## Origin / follow-up

Follows and completes #101513.

- **Anchor:** #101513 fixed exec auto-reviewer rationale truncation by using UTF-16-safe truncation.
- **Gap this fills:** `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts` still used raw `slice()` for retained stdout/stderr in the extension/custom-tool command execution path.
- **Consistency:** This patch reuses the existing `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` helper instead of introducing another truncation implementation.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

I checked current open PRs and issues for the same `execCommand` / extension exec UTF-16 truncation gap.

- No open issue matched `extension exec output UTF-16 surrogate` or `execCommand truncation surrogate`.
- No open PR matched `execCommand truncation UTF-16 safe`.
- One open PR mentions surrogate-safe truncation in a different memory-core dreaming snippet path; it does not touch `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts` or the extension exec stdout/stderr retention path.
- **Related open PR scan:** no same-file or same-runtime duplicate was found for this patch.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** extension/custom-tool exec retained stdout/stderr must not contain dangling UTF-16 surrogate halves after truncation.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** extension command output is user-triggered text that can be returned as stdout/stderr; a split surrogate can show replacement characters or invalid text to the next consumer.
- **Canonical reachability path:** user-triggered extension command output input → child-process pipe ingestion and Buffer-to-string type conversion in `execCommand` → `ExecResult` runtime object → retained stdout/stderr returned as the command effect.
- **Boundary crossed:** child-process stdout/stderr pipe payloads are captured through the same `execCommand` retention logic used by extension command execution.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** existing repository helper `sliceUtf16Safe` is reused; provider-specific constraints are not applicable to this local command-output boundary.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `appendCapturedOutput` is the source-of-truth retention boundary for `ExecResult` stdout/stderr caps. The patch fixes the invariant there instead of adding a downstream cleanup step, so stored/returned command output share the same safe retained text.
- **Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw repo on Node/Vitest using the shipped child-process output capture boundary.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/sessions/exec.test.ts
```

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module
# Imported src/agents/sessions/exec.ts, executed a child process that wrote
# A😀B to stdout and C😀D to stderr, and called execCommand(..., { maxOutputChars: 2 }).
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/sessions/exec.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  7 passed (7)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 11.57s
```

```json
{
  "stdout": "B",
  "stderr": "D",
  "stdoutLength": 1,
  "stderrLength": 1,
  "stdoutCodes": ["42"],
  "stderrCodes": ["44"],
  "stdoutDangling": [],
  "stderrDangling": [],
  "stdoutTruncatedChars": 3,
  "stderrTruncatedChars": 3,
  "code": 0
}
```

- **Observed result after fix:** stdout and stderr retain valid text with no dangling surrogate halves; truncation counts reflect the actual removed UTF-16 code units.
- **What was not tested:** full dev gateway startup was not run because the changed boundary is the local `execCommand` child-process output capture path.
- **What did NOT change:** no extension loader API, process spawning, timeout, abort, process-tree cleanup, model routing, or network behavior changed.
- **Target test file:** `src/agents/sessions/exec.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** caller-capped stdout `A😀B` and stderr `C😀D` with `maxOutputChars: 2` now retain `B` and `D` without dangling surrogate halves; the default output-limit path also avoids retaining a half emoji at the cap boundary.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** the regression hits `execCommand` at the retained-output source-of-truth boundary, covers both stdout and stderr, and also covers the default limit path where the same helper is now used.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High. The diff is limited to two slicing call sites plus focused tests, and fresh verification is bound to the committed diff.
- **Patch quality notes:** Patch quality warning considered: this is not a fallback, default-value change, catch/ignore path, or downstream masking step; it replaces unsafe slicing at the retention source.

## Review findings addressed

No maintainer review findings are attached to this follow-up yet. This patch addresses the sibling gap left by #101513 in the extension exec output retention path.

## Regression Test Plan

```bash
node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/sessions/exec.test.ts
```

The regression suite now covers:

- caller-capped retained stdout/stderr containing emoji at the truncation boundary;
- default output-limit truncation when the cap would otherwise split an emoji surrogate pair;
- existing independent stdout/stderr retention, process-tree cleanup, timeout, and stream-error behavior.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** no merge-risk label is expected for this XS scoped agents/runtime retention patch; changed files are `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts` and `src/agents/sessions/exec.test.ts` only.
- **Risk explanation:** retained output can become one UTF-16 code unit shorter at a surrogate boundary, but caps remain enforced and returned text becomes valid rather than partially split.
- **Why acceptable:** this preserves the existing API and truncation behavior while enforcing the text-validity invariant already used by the shared helper.

## Risk / Compatibility

Risk is low and localized to retained output truncation in `execCommand`.

- API shape is unchanged.
- Output caps remain enforced.
- At a surrogate boundary, retained output may be one UTF-16 code unit shorter than the raw cap to avoid returning invalid text.
- `stdoutTruncatedChars` and `stderrTruncatedChars` now count the actual number of removed UTF-16 code units after safe slicing.

## What was not changed

- No extension loader API changes.
- No process spawning, timeout, abort, or process-tree cleanup behavior changes.
- No model routing or network behavior changes.
- No new truncation helper was added.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** `execCommand` used raw `String.prototype.slice()` to enforce retained output caps. JavaScript slicing is based on UTF-16 code units, so slicing at a cap boundary can return only one half of a surrogate pair.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The fix replaces both affected slicing sites in `appendCapturedOutput` with the shared UTF-16-safe helper, covering tail retention for caller-supplied caps and head retention for default output-limit enforcement at the source where retained stdout/stderr is produced.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(auth): use sanitized profile name for Codex import even without id- prefix
target.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **AI-Assisted Contribution:** This PR was prepared and validated with the assistance of an AI coding assistant (Antigravity/Gemini).

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes an issue where If `accountId` is missing, the function only accepts `profileName` if it starts with `"id-"` (which is the case for subject-based names, not email-based names). If `profileName` is an email (e.g. `user@example.com`), it does not start with `"id-"`, so the function falls back to a static `fallback` string (e.g. `"hermes-import"`). When migrating multiple credentials, they will all share the same fallback profile name, causing migrations to collide or overwrite each other..

## Why This Change Was Made
Sanitize and return the profile name (such as emails) even if it doesn't start with `"id-"`:
```javascript
function resolveOpenAICodexImportProfileName(identity, fallback) {
if (identity.accountId) return `account-${identity.accountId.replaceAll(/[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+/gu, "-")}`;
if (identity.profileName) return identity.profileName.replaceAll(/[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+/gu, "-");
return fallback;
}
```


## User Impact
When migrating OpenAI Codex profiles (e.g. from Hermes), stable identity details like the profile email should be used to construct a unique, sanitized profile name if `accountId` is not present, avoiding name collisions.

## Evidence

### Unit Tests / Verification Suite
- Branch: `fix/1.5-codex-import-profile-name-collision`
- Commit: `85395a0003`
- Test command: `pnpm test src/plugin-sdk/provider-openai-chatgpt-auth.test.ts`

target.title: fix(diagnostics-otel): set CLIENT span kind on model call and tool execution spans
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

All OpenClaw trace spans use `SpanKind.INTERNAL` by default, making external API calls (LLM providers, tool executions) invisible as distinct dependency nodes in distributed tracing tools. Model call spans (model.call.*) only got `CLIENT` kind when the `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental` opt-in was set; tool execution spans (tool.execution.*) never carried an explicit kind at all.

- Problem: Trace visualization tools (Jaeger, Zipkin) show all spans as flat internal operations — no way to distinguish network latency from processing time
- Solution: Set `SpanKind.CLIENT` unconditionally on model call spans and on actual tool execution spans (started/completed/error). Blocked tool spans (policy-denied, no outgoing request) keep the implicit `INTERNAL` default.
- What changed: `extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.ts` (modelCallSpanKind + 3 actual tool span sites; blocked path unchanged), `service.test.ts` (updated assertions + blocked span test), `docs/gateway/opentelemetry.md` (docs reflect kind is no longer gated)
- What did NOT change: GenAI semconv span naming/attributes remain gated behind `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN`; model.failover, context.assembled, and other internal-only spans keep their existing kind behavior

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #102017
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

The OpenTelemetry SpanKind specification defines `CLIENT` for outgoing requests to external services. LLM API calls (OpenAI, xAI, Ollama, etc.) and tool executions (shell commands, HTTP requests, filesystem operations) semantically represent client requests. Using `INTERNAL` for these spans breaks distributed tracing — latency analysis cannot distinguish network round-trips from internal processing, and dependency graphs in Jaeger/Zipkin cannot show external service dependencies.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Model call and tool execution spans now carry `SpanKind.CLIENT` (value 2) instead of the default `SpanKind.INTERNAL`
- Real environment tested: Linux Node 24, branch `fix/otel-span-kind-client-102017`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
# Run the full test suite
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.9

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  108 passed (108)

# Source-level verification:

# modelCallSpanKind() now unconditionally returns CLIENT:
$ grep -A 3 "function modelCallSpanKind" extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.ts
function modelCallSpanKind(): SpanKind {
  return SpanKind.CLIENT;
}

# 3 actual tool.execution span creation points carry kind=CLIENT:
$ grep -B 1 "kind: SpanKind.CLIENT" extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.ts
            kind: SpanKind.CLIENT,    # tool.execution.started
            kind: SpanKind.CLIENT,    # tool.execution.completed
            kind: SpanKind.CLIENT,    # tool.execution.error

# Blocked tool span has no explicit kind (INTERNAL default):
$ grep -A 5 "outcome.*blocked" extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.ts | grep -c "kind"
0

# Assertions verifying the span kind values:
$ grep -B 1 "kind).toBe" extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts
expect(modelOptions?.kind).toBe(2);                  # model call span
expect(toolOptions?.kind).toBe(2);                   # tool execution span
expect(Object.hasOwn(blockedOptions ?? {}, "kind")).toBe(false);  # blocked span
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. Model call spans (model.call.submitted/completed/error) always export with `SpanKind.CLIENT` — no longer gated behind `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN`
  2. Actual tool execution spans (tool.execution.started/completed/error) always export with `SpanKind.CLIENT`
  3. Blocked tool spans (policy-denied, no outgoing request) keep `SpanKind.INTERNAL` — semantically correct
  4. GenAI semconv env var continues to control span naming (openclaw.model.call vs gen_ai.*) independently
  5. Internal-only spans (model.failover, context.assembled, memory.pressure, session.stuck) remain `SpanKind.INTERNAL`
- What was not tested: Live Jaeger/Zipkin collector ingestion (requires external infrastructure).
- Real OTel exporter proof via `ConsoleSpanExporter` (production OTel SDK, not mocked):

```console
--- Span 1: openclaw.model.call ---
kind: 2 (SpanKind.CLIENT)  ← PR sets this unconditionally

--- Span 2: openclaw.tool.execution ---
kind: 2 (SpanKind.CLIENT)  ← PR sets this on actual exec spans

--- Span 3: openclaw.tool.execution (blocked) ---
kind: 0 (SpanKind.INTERNAL) ← PR keeps default, no explicit kind set
```

The exported JSON from real `@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-node` + `ConsoleSpanExporter` confirms:
- `openclaw.model.call` → **kind=2 (CLIENT)** — correct for LLM API calls
- `openclaw.tool.execution` (actual) → **kind=2 (CLIENT)** — correct for outgoing tool requests
- `openclaw.tool.execution` (blocked) → **kind=0 (INTERNAL)** — correct, no HTTP request was made

```json
{"name":"openclaw.model.call","kind":2,"attributes":{"gen_ai.operation.name":"chat","gen_ai.request.model":"gpt-5.5"}}
{"name":"openclaw.tool.execution","kind":2,"attributes":{"tool.name":"browser","tool.source":"mcp"}}
{"name":"openclaw.tool.execution","kind":0,"attributes":{"tool.name":"browser","tool.source":"mcp","openclaw.tool.blocked":"true"}}
```

## Root Cause (if applicable)

PR #86191 (`f824e1596ad`) introduced `modelCallSpanKind()` which only returned `SpanKind.CLIENT` when `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental` was set, otherwise `undefined` → `INTERNAL`. Tool execution spans were added without any kind override since their introduction.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

The test suite (`service.test.ts`) has four assertions specific to span kind:
- Default model call: `expect(modelOptions?.kind).toBe(2)` (was `toBe(false)` for absent kind)
- Tool execution (error path): `expect(toolOptions?.kind).toBe(2)` (new)
- Tool execution (content capture): `expect(toolOptions?.kind).toBe(2)` (new)
- Blocked tool span: `expect(Object.hasOwn(blockedOptions ?? {}, "kind")).toBe(false)` (new, focused test)

108 tests pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None directly visible to end users. Trace data consumers (Jaeger, Zipkin, Grafana Tempo, Datadog) will see `kind=CLIENT` on model call and tool execution spans, enabling proper dependency graphs and latency breakdown.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Source-level verification of all relevant span creation points; test assertion updates checked for correctness
- Edge cases checked: GenAI semconv opt-in still controls span names/attributes independently; tool spans that go through the trusted span tracking path (takeTrackedTrustedSpan) inherit the same kind from the original span
- What you did NOT verify: Live Jaeger collector round-trip; non-Node runtimes

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — span kind change only affects how trace backends classify spans, not runtime behavior
- [x] Config/env changes? Only the documentation of `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN` — no actual config surface changed
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. Unconditional CLIENT for model calls + CLIENT for actual tool executions, blocked tool spans kept INTERNAL. No new config or env var needed.
- **Refactor needed**: No. The changes are self-contained in 5 locations within one file.
- **Alternative considered**: Keeping the GenAI-semconv gate but changing span kind to always be CLIENT regardless of naming — this is what we implemented. Another option was adding a new config knob for span kind per span type, which would be over-engineered for this use case.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: None significant. SpanKind is a classification tag on exported spans — changing from INTERNAL to CLIENT affects trace visualization only, not runtime behavior, data paths, or permission checks.
- **Mitigation**: All existing span names, attributes, and lifecycle are preserved. The change is opt-in only at the trace-consumer level (users who export traces to Jaeger/Zipkin will see the improvement).
- **Compatibility**: Users currently ingesting OpenClaw traces who have built dashboards/filters based on `kind=INTERNAL` will need to update those filters. No users have reported relying on the INTERNAL kind value.

Fixes #102017

target.title: fix(cron): keep system event queued when main-session heartbeat is disabled
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: When a cron job fires `sessionTarget: "main"` with `payload.kind: "systemEvent"` and default `wakeMode: "now"`, if the main-session heartbeat returns a non-retryable skip (e.g. `"disabled"`), the already-enqueued system event was removed and the job returned `status: "skipped"`. The event was silently lost — never delivered to the user.

**Solution**: Two-layer fix — (1) Timer layer: keep system event queued for retryable outcomes, remove for non-retryable; (2) Heartbeat layer: bypass per-agent heartbeat config gates for cron-sourced wakes.

**What changed**:

- `src/cron/service/timer.ts`: In `executeMainSessionCronJob()`, the two branches that called `removeQueuedSystemEventHandle()` on heartbeat skip/error are replaced with a single branch. For retryable skips (busy), the event stays queued with a background heartbeat request. For non-retryable outcomes (global-disable, quiet-hours, no-tasks-due, failures), the queued event is removed to prevent permanent stranding since the wake layer only retries busy skips.

- `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts`:
  - `runHeartbeatOnce()`: Wraps the `isHeartbeatEnabledForAgent()` and `resolveHeartbeatIntervalMs()` checks in `if (opts.source !== "cron")` — only non-cron sources are gated by per-agent config.
  - Scheduler `run()`: When a cron-targeted wake targets an agent not present in the heartbeat scheduler's agent list, calls `runOnce()` directly instead of returning `{status: "skipped", reason: "disabled"}`.

**What did NOT change**: The heartbeat-`"ran"` path (the common happy path) is untouched. No new dependencies, no config changes, no API surface changes.

Fixes #101537

---

## What Problem This Solves

System events like reminders, scheduled messages, and periodic notifications were silently lost when the main session heartbeat was disabled — a common state when the user hasn't interacted recently. The design flaw was coupling event delivery to immediate wake success.

Two layers contributed:
1. The timer layer was too eager to discard already-enqueued events when heartbeat failed
2. The heartbeat layer's per-agent config gates treated cron-sourced wakes the same as regular heartbeats, even though cron manages its own retry and scheduling policy

---

## Root Cause

**Layer 1 — Timer layer**: The system event was enqueued before the heartbeat attempt (line ~1990). When heartbeat failed, the cleanup code removed the event — discarding work already done.

**Layer 2 — Heartbeat layer**: `runHeartbeatOnce()` checked `isHeartbeatEnabledForAgent()` and `resolveHeartbeatIntervalMs()` unconditionally. Agents without explicit heartbeat config (e.g., `{id: "main"}` without `heartbeat: {every: ...}`) would always return `skipped/disabled` — even when the wake was triggered by cron. Additionally, the scheduler's `run()` returned `skipped/disabled` when the target agent was not in `state.agents` (agents without explicit heartbeat config are not tracked by the scheduler).

Together these two layers caused cron→main system event deliveries to fail silently on every attempt.

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Keep system event queued when main-session heartbeat returns skipped/error; request background heartbeat instead of removing event. Bypass per-agent heartbeat config gates for cron-sourced wakes. Preserve skipped/error status so one-shot retry behavior and job visibility are maintained.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64 / Node.js v24.1.0 / OpenClaw `fix/issue-101537-cron-main-systemevent-skip-disabled`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx vitest run` targeted test commands as shown below, each exercising real production functions at L2 level (real `runHeartbeatOnce`, real system event queue, real CronJob objects).

**After-fix evidence**:

L2+ evidence (real function calls, real objects, real system event queue):
```
$ npx vitest run src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts -t "does not return disabled for cron"
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 43 skipped (44)

$ npx vitest run src/infra/heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts -t "routes cron targeted wakes"
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 25 skipped (26)

$ npx vitest run src/cron/service.main-job-passes-heartbeat-target-last.test.ts -t "does not skip with"
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 3 skipped (4)

$ node --import tsx -e 'import { isHeartbeatEnabledForAgent } from "./src/infra/heartbeat-summary.js"; console.log(isHeartbeatEnabledForAgent({agents:{list:[{id:"worker", heartbeat:{every:"5m"}}, {id:"main"}]}}, "main"));'
false  ← gate rejects main; both fix layers now bypass this for cron

$ npx tsx evidence/pr-101668/run-evidence.mjs
=== L2 Evidence ===
1. System event enqueued, events in queue before: 1
2. applyJobResult called with status="skipped", error="disabled"
   shouldDelete: false (delete only on "ok")
   job.state.lastStatus: skipped, lastError: disabled
   Job in store: YES
3. Events in queue after: 1 (preserved)
```

Full regression suites:
```
$ pnpm test -- src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  44 passed (44)

$ pnpm test -- src/infra/heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  26 passed (26)

$ pnpm test -- src/cron/service.runs-one-shot-main-job-disables-it.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  14 passed (14)

$ pnpm test -- src/cron/service.main-job-passes-heartbeat-target-last.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  3 passed (3)

$ pnpm test -- src/cron/service.jobs.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  78 passed (78)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: Cron-sourced `runHeartbeatOnce` no longer returns `disabled` for agents without explicit heartbeat config; heartbeat scheduler routes cron-targeted wakes directly to `runOnce()`; system events are preserved through disabled-heartbeat scenarios; the job retains skipped status; background heartbeat is requested for deferred delivery.

**What was not tested**: Real Gateway + cron daemon integration is not tested here. The fix is exercised through unit tests with real production functions (Vitest test framework) for the heartbeat runner, and injected dependencies for the cron timer. The complete multi-hop delivery path (heartbeat gate bypass → queue preservation → deferred delivery) is covered by the combined test suites.

---

## Tests and validation

### Unit tests

Test coverage:
- ✓ keeps system event queued when disabled-heartbeat one-shot cannot wake
- ✓ disables one-shot when disabled-heartbeat retry is exhausted
- ✓ does not return disabled for cron source when agent has no explicit heartbeat config
- ✓ routes cron targeted wakes to agents without explicit heartbeat config in scheduler
- ✓ cron main job does not skip with 'disabled' when agent has no heartbeat config
- ✓ removes queued system event for non-retryable heartbeat outcomes (global-disable, quiet-hours, no-tasks-due)
- ✓ does not strand events permanently for non-retryable outcomes

### CI

CI has a pre-existing failure in `checks-node-compact-small-whole-2` unrelated to this change. All 71 other CI checks pass.

---

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation

**Merge risk**: Low. The behavioral changes are scoped to:
1. The heartbeat-skip/error path in `executeMainSessionCronJob()` — non-ok heartbeats for cron jobs no longer discard the enqueued event (for retryable outcomes); non-retryable outcomes still remove the event to prevent stranding
2. Cron-sourced `runHeartbeatOnce` calls — bypass per-agent config gates, preserving the global disable gate
3. Cron-targeted scheduler wakes — agents not in the scheduler's state are run directly instead of returning disabled

Global gate `areHeartbeatsEnabled()` is preserved for all sources. No new deps, no config or API changes. Rollback is a revert of this branch's commits.

**ClawSweeper P1 addressed**:
1. ✅ "Keep disabled cron wakes visible" — returning non-ok status keeps the job in the store with skipped/error state
2. ✅ "For deleteAfterRun one-shots, returning ok removes job immediately" — now returns "skipped", preserving retry behavior
3. ✅ "Add real behavior proof" — L2 evidence with real function calls showing event preservation, heartbeat gate bypass, and scheduler routing for cron sources
4. ✅ "Fix stale per-run queue and disabled heartbeat gate behavior" — by bypassing `isHeartbeatEnabledForAgent()` and `resolveHeartbeatIntervalMs()` for cron sources, plus direct `runOnce()` routing in the scheduler
5. ✅ "Remove non-retryable cron events instead of stranding them" — non-retryable outcomes (global-disable, quiet-hours, no-tasks-due, failures) now call `removeQueuedSystemEventHandle()` since the wake layer only retries busy skips

## Current review state

- [x] Self-review completed
- [ ] At least one maintainer review
- [ ] All CI checks passed

## AI-assisted

This PR was created with AI assistance for code understanding, root cause analysis, test restructuring, and PR body generation. Human review was applied to all AI-generated code and tests.

target.title: fix(infra): guard channel ingress queue parseJson against corrupted JSON
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a single corrupted `payload_json`, `metadata_json`, or `completed_metadata_json` row in the SQLite channel ingress queue crashes the entire queue operation. The `parseJson()` helper calls `JSON.parse(value)` without a try-catch. A corrupt row throws an uncaught `SyntaxError` that propagates through `baseRecord()` (called by `listPending`, `listClaims`, `claimNext`, `enqueue`) and `completedRecord()` (called by `enqueue` duplicate detection). One bad row in `listPending()` or `listClaims()` kills **all** entries in that listing. This affects every channel that uses the durable ingress queue for inbound message processing.

Additionally, `claimNext` and `claim` would UPDATE a pending row to `claimed` status **before** validating the payload could be decoded — so a corrupt payload could become an invisible claimed row, hidden from `listPending`/`listClaims`/`recoverStaleClaims`, permanently blocking queue recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. **Tagged parse result**: `parseJson()` now returns `{ ok: true, value } | { ok: false }` instead of the ambiguous `unknown | null`. `JSON.parse("null")` is valid and returns `null`, which the old sentinel conflated with parse failure. The tagged result cleanly separates "valid JSON value" from "corrupt input".

2. **Guard `parseJson` at the chokepoint**: `baseRecord()` returns `null` when `payload_json` is corrupt (unrecoverable). Corrupt `metadata_json`/`completed_metadata_json` is non-fatal — the record is kept with metadata omitted. All callers (`listPending`, `listClaims`, `enqueue`, `claimNext`, `claim`) handle null/omitted results.

3. **Validate before claiming**: `claimNext` calls `baseRecord()` inside `rows.find()` to skip corrupt rows before they are selected, and `claim` pre-reads the pending row and validates `baseRecord()` before issuing the UPDATE. No corrupt row can ever be promoted to `claimed` status.

4. **Tombstone corrupt rows on duplicate enqueue**: When `enqueue()` finds a duplicate event whose existing row has a corrupt `payload_json`, it now tombstones the corrupt row as `failed` with reason `"corrupt_payload"` instead of throwing. The caller receives `{ kind: "failed", duplicate: true }`.

5. **Recover corrupt claimed rows during stale recovery**: `recoverStaleClaims()` now scans raw claimed rows directly (bypassing `listClaims()` which filters out corrupt rows). Corrupt claimed rows are tombstoned as `failed` instead of being left permanently invisible to recovery.

## User Impact

No user-visible impact under normal operation. When a channel ingress queue row is somehow corrupted:
- `listPending` / `listClaims` skip the bad entry instead of crashing
- `claimNext` / `claim` skip corrupt rows and claim the next valid one
- `enqueue` duplicate detection tombstones corrupt rows and returns a proper result
- `recoverStaleClaims` tombstones corrupt claimed rows so they don't block the queue
- Valid JSON `null` payload is correctly preserved (not treated as corrupt)

## Real behavior proof

- **Real environment:** Linux, Node v22.22.0, driving real `createChannelIngressQueue` against a real on-disk SQLite database.
- **Exact PR head:** `93572a00b0`.
- **Evidence after fix (25 tests, all pass):**

```text
      Tests  25 passed (25)
```

New tests cover: pending row with corrupt `payload_json` → skipped, corrupt `metadata_json` → metadata omitted, corrupt claimed row → skipped in `listClaims`, corrupt `completed_metadata_json` → duplicate detection works, `claimNext` skips corrupt pending → claims next valid, `claim` rejects corrupt pending, valid JSON null → preserved, duplicate enqueue of corrupt row → tombstoned as failed, stale recovery of corrupt claimed row → tombstoned as failed.

target.title: fix(bug): Google Chat stale approval cards keep retrying after approv…
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Google Chat approval card clicks treat `APPROVAL_NOT_FOUND` gateway errors the same as transient failures. When a user clicks a stale/expired approval card after the backing approval was already resolved or deleted elsewhere, the click handler incorrectly releases the card token for retry instead of consuming it.

**Concrete problem**: Users can repeatedly click the same expired approval card, causing the gateway to receive multiple resolution attempts for an approval that no longer exists. Each click appears to "work" (returns `true`) but the gateway logs show repeated `APPROVAL_NOT_FOUND` errors for the same approval ID.

**Reproduction**:
1. Register a Google Chat approval card binding
2. Click the card after the approval was resolved/expired elsewhere
3. Gateway returns `APPROVAL_NOT_FOUND`
4. Click the same stale card again → retry loop

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix distinguishes between **terminal errors** (approval no longer exists) and **transient errors** (gateway temporarily unavailable):

- **`APPROVAL_NOT_FOUND`** → Terminal state: consume the token, log that the approval is expired/stale, and return `handled` without retrying
- **Other errors** → Transient: release the token for retry and re-throw the error

The change was made in `extensions/googlechat/src/approval-card-click.ts:86-98` by adding a type check in the catch block:

```typescript
catch (error) {
  if (isApprovalNotFoundError(error)) {
    // Terminal state: approval no longer exists. Consume the token and ignore future clicks.
    completeGoogleChatApprovalCardBinding(token);
    params.target.runtime.log?.(
      `[${params.target.account.accountId}] googlechat approval expired/stale id=${consumed.approvalId} decision=${consumed.decision}`,
    );
    return true;
  }
  // Transient error: release for retry.
  releaseGoogleChatApprovalCardBinding(token);
  throw error;
}
```

This follows the same pattern used by other approval channels (Telegram, Matrix, Signal, etc.) which already handle `APPROVAL_NOT_FOUND` as a terminal condition.

## User Impact

**Google Chat users**: Expired/stale approval cards now fail gracefully on first click instead of creating a retry loop. Users will see a log message indicating the approval has expired, and subsequent clicks on the same card are silently ignored.

**Operators/Admins**: Gateway logs will no longer show repeated `APPROVAL_NOT_FOUND` errors for the same approval ID from stale card clicks.

**No breaking changes**: The fix only affects error handling behavior. Successful approval flows remain unchanged.

## Evidence

### Test Run

```bash
pnpm test extensions/googlechat/src/approval-card-click.test.ts
```

 RUN  v4.1.8 /home/0668001433/python_project/openclaw

 ✓  extension-messaging  extensions/googlechat/src/approval-card-click.test.ts (7 tests) 31ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)

### Related Files

- **Test**: `extensions/googlechat/src/approval-card-click.test.ts:291-332` (existing test validates the fix)
