target.title: fix(agents): pause yielded main-session runs
target.body:
## Summary

Extend the subagent yield-pause fix from [6f3b5f86](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6f3b5f8666f3a3877b62d9019b8842455fdf62e1) to top-level (non-subagent) sessions.

When a main session ends via the `sessions_yield` tool, the runner already emits a lifecycle event with `yielded: true` and `livenessState: "paused"`. The runner's terminal lifecycle metadata, the agent-job snapshot cache, and the agent.wait dedupe entry all propagate those flags generically, so subagent and non-subagent runs benefit equally from those parts of 6f3b5f86.

The gap is in `gateway/session-lifecycle-state.ts`. `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` does not look at the `yielded` flag, so the session entry is persisted with `status: \"done\"` even though the runner has queued a post-yield continuation that drains on the next turn. Dashboards, restart recovery, and follow-up turns then treat the session as finished and race the continuation, producing the in-context overflow and out-of-order events the user reports.

## Why the same fix needs to apply to the top-level session

The subagent registry tracks active subagent runs in memory and uses `pauseReason: \"sessions_yield\"` to keep yielded entries in a paused state instead of marking them complete. The main session has no equivalent in-memory registry; its lifecycle state is persisted directly through `persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent` into the on-disk session entry. The gap shows up in three places:

1. The persisted session entry says `status: \"done\"`, so `sessions_list`, `sessions.changed` broadcasts, and dashboard UI all show the session as finished.
2. `main-session-restart-recovery` is keyed off `entry.abortedLastRun` and `entry.status === \"running\"`. With status=done it leaves the entry alone, but on a clean restart-mid-yield the yielded session can also end up `abortedLastRun=true` (the cleaned-lock path), at which point recovery would force a `[System] Your previous turn was interrupted...` resume that races the queued continuation.
3. A new user message arrives at a session that is internally paused but externally \"done\" — the gateway dispatches a fresh agent.run, and the queued steered yield-interrupt drains alongside the new user input, producing out-of-order assistant text.

## Shape of the change

- Recognize the lifecycle `yielded` flag in `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` and derive `status: \"paused\"` with `pauseReason: \"sessions_yield\"` instead of `done`. Yielded short-circuits before the `aborted`/`stopReason` branches so partial classifications cannot mask the paused state.
- Clear `pauseReason` on the next lifecycle `start` event so a fresh run reactivates the session, mirroring how `subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts` clears `pauseReason` on completion.
- Add `\"paused\"` to `SessionRunStatus` in both `gateway/session-utils.types.ts` and `agents/tools/sessions-helpers.ts`, and add `pauseReason?: \"sessions_yield\"` to `SessionEntry` and `GatewaySessionRow`.
- Surface `pauseReason` on the `sessions.changed` broadcast snapshot and the `loadGatewaySessionRow` builder so consumers (UI, sessions_list tool) see the paused state.
- Tighten `isTerminalSessionStatus` so the type predicate stays accurate after \"paused\" joins the union (paused is not terminal).
- Skip `main-session-restart-recovery` for entries with `pauseReason: \"sessions_yield\"` so they are not re-prompted with the generic interrupted-turn message.

The runner-level changes (yieldDetected -> livenessState=paused/yielded=true) and the gateway agent-job/agent-wait-dedupe propagation that 6f3b5f86 already added are unchanged. This PR plugs the missing seam between those generic signals and the persisted session entry.

## Test coverage

- `src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts`:
  - `marks yielded lifecycle end events as paused with sessions_yield reason` (persisted patch).
  - `treats yielded as paused even when aborted is set` (yield short-circuit).
  - `clears pauseReason when a fresh run starts on a paused session` (start-phase reactivation).
  - Existing terminal-mapping tests updated to include explicit `pauseReason: undefined` on non-yield ends.
- `src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts`:
  - `skips sessions paused via sessions_yield instead of forcing a resume`.
  - `does not mark sessions with sessions_yield pauseReason as restart-aborted from cleaned locks`.

## Local validation

- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — clean.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts src/gateway/server-chat.agent-events.test.ts src/config/sessions.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-list-tool.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.create-event.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent-wait-dedupe.test.ts src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts src/agents/subagent-announce-output.test.ts src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts` — all green (235 tests).
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `pnpm format:docs:check`, `pnpm check:changelog-attributions` — all clean on changed files.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on \`fix(agents): pause yielded main-session runs\`.
- [ ] Manual smoke: trigger `sessions_yield` from a main-session conversation; confirm the session entry persists `status: paused` and `pauseReason: sessions_yield`, and that a follow-up turn flips back to `running` with `pauseReason: undefined`.
- [ ] Restart-recovery smoke: kill the gateway while a main session is paused via yield; confirm restart-recovery skips it instead of re-prompting with the interrupted-turn message.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: Before this PR, when a top-level (non-subagent) embedded `openclaw` run ended via the `sessions_yield` tool, the runner emitted `yielded=true` and `livenessState=paused` but the gateway treated it as a clean completion and wrote `status=done`. The session displayed as finished while awaiting a queued post-yield continuation, racing dashboards, restart-recovery, and follow-up turns. After this PR, the lifecycle persistence derives `status=paused` with `pauseReason=sessions_yield`, restart-recovery skips paused sessions, and `SessionRunStatus` adds `"paused"` so consumers can distinguish a yielded run from a completed one.
- **Real environment tested**: live OpenClaw gateway on rh-bot.lan, pid 65734, build SHA 23804e610c (upgrade-v2026.5.28 with this PR cherry-picked). The deployed `dist/server-chat-*.js` and `dist/main-session-restart-recovery-*.js` chunks carry the new `pauseReason`/`sessions_yield` logic; the proof script imports and executes those exact bundle bytes.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```bash
  # On rh-bot.lan, confirm deployed bundles carry the PR logic:
  grep -c 'sessions_yield\|pauseReason' \
    /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/main-session-restart-recovery-CirHJY3p.js
  # -> 1 (the new shouldSkipMainRecovery branch)

  grep -c 'sessions_yield\|pauseReason' \
    /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/server-chat-D9hpq-gf.js
  # -> non-zero (new deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot branches)

  # Drive the deployed code with three scenarios:
  node /tmp/proof-75662-amittell.mjs
  ```
  Proof script (`/tmp/proof-75662-amittell.mjs`) extracts the deployed
  `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` from `server-chat-D9hpq-gf.js` via
  `vm.runInContext`, dynamically imports `main-session-restart-recovery-CirHJY3p.js`
  to grab the exported `markRestartAbortedMainSessions`, seeds a temp
  state-dir with one yielded and one non-yielded `running` entry, and asserts
  three behaviors:
  1. Lifecycle `phase=end` with `yielded=true` -> `status=paused`,
     `pauseReason=sessions_yield`, `abortedLastRun=false`.
  2. Same entry passed to restart-recovery is SKIPPED (no `abortedLastRun`
     write, `updatedAt` unchanged).
  3. Sibling running entry without `pauseReason` is marked
     `abortedLastRun=true` (existing behavior preserved).
  Plus a guard check: lifecycle `phase=error` with `yielded=true` returns
  `status=failed` with NO `pauseReason` leak.
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  === PR #75662 real-behavior proof ===
  host=rh-bot.lan pid=84884 node=v25.8.2
  dist=/Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist

  [1] lifecycle bundle: /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/server-chat-D9hpq-gf.js
  [1a] yielded terminal -> {"updatedAt":1780285520789,"status":"paused","startedAt":1780285519789,"endedAt":1780285520789,"runtimeMs":1000,"abortedLastRun":false,"pauseReason":"sessions_yield"}
  [1a] OK: paused status carries pauseReason=sessions_yield
  [1b] non-yielded terminal -> {"updatedAt":1780285520789,"status":"done","startedAt":1780285519789,"endedAt":1780285520789,"runtimeMs":1000,"abortedLastRun":false}
  [1b] OK: non-yielded run preserves status=done with no pauseReason
  [1c] error+yielded -> {"updatedAt":1780285520789,"status":"failed","startedAt":1780285519789,"endedAt":1780285520789,"runtimeMs":1000,"abortedLastRun":false}
  [1c] OK: error phase masks yielded marker, no pauseReason leak

  [2] seeded /var/folders/cn/.../state/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json
  [2] recovery bundle: /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/main-session-restart-recovery-CirHJY3p.js
  [2] exports: i, n, r, t
  [main-session-restart-recovery] marked 1 interrupted main session(s) for restart recovery (pr-75662-proof)
  [2] mark result: {"marked":1,"skipped":1}
  [2] yielded entry after: {"sessionId":"sess-yielded","status":"running","pauseReason":"sessions_yield","startedAt":...,"updatedAt":1780285519789}
  [2] normal entry after:  {"sessionId":"sess-normal","status":"running","startedAt":...,"updatedAt":1780285521266,"abortedLastRun":true}
  [2a] OK: yielded session was skipped (no abortedLastRun, no updatedAt bump)
  [2b] OK: non-yielded running session was marked abortedLastRun=true

  === ALL PROOFS PASSED ===
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: All three scenarios pass on the deployed bundle. A yielded terminal event produces `status=paused`/`pauseReason=sessions_yield` and is skipped by restart recovery (no `abortedLastRun` mutation, no `updatedAt` bump). A non-yielded terminal event still produces `status=done` with no `pauseReason` (existing behavior preserved). An error phase masks the `yielded` flag and reports `status=failed` with no `pauseReason` leak, matching the gating comment in `resolveTerminalStatus`.
- **Targeted tests**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts` -> 22 passed + 15 passed (37/37). Broader: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts src/gateway/session-message-events.test.ts` -> 172/172 passed. `node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs --only=core --threads=4` -> clean.
- **What was not tested**: End-to-end live channel trigger (sending a real Telegram message that drives `sessions_yield` to completion); this is exercised by the existing vitest coverage in `pi-embedded-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts` rather than reproduced live on rh-bot.


## Live exact-head capture (2026-06-12): found and fixed an emit-side gap

Running the requested live scenario on an isolated sandbox gateway (loopback :28795, fresh `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, Control UI webchat, native `openai-completions` lane with a tool-calling model) surfaced a real defect in this PR's original head: **the paused state never persisted in live runs, on any lane.** A store probe polling every 0.3s across four real `sessions_spawn` + `sessions_yield` turns at head `be96a422ff` captured the persisted row going `running -> killed` with `abortedLastRun: true` at yield time -- the exact pre-PR failure this PR exists to prevent.

**Root cause (probe-instrumented):** `sessions_yield` aborts the attempt mid-stream (`runAbortController.abort("sessions_yield")`), and the terminal lifecycle event can be emitted from the abort teardown before `run.ts` post-processing writes the `yielded` meta. The bundle-level instrumentation captured the failing ordering directly:

```
emitLifecycleTerminal state.yielded = undefined  aborted = false   <- event emitted first
meta.yielded set -> false                                          <- run.ts wrote 551ms later
```

The event reaches `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` carrying `aborted` without `yielded`, and `resolveTerminalStatus` correctly resolves killed. The projection/recovery/UI logic this PR adds was never the problem; the emit side never fed it. The unit tests passed because they fabricate events that already carry `yielded: true`.

**Fix (in `a46ba508b8`):** `onYield` now records `yielded` through the subscription's terminal lifecycle meta channel at tool time, before the abort, using the same late-binding pattern the yield abort itself uses (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`). A regression test pins the handler half: an end event with `state.yielded` set and `aborted` resolved from the `isTerminalAborted` fallback still carries `yielded` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.lifecycle.test.ts`).

**Post-fix live proof, end to end (same sandbox, instrumented bundle):**

```
10:27:40.065  [PROBE] meta.yielded set -> true              (onYield records at tool time)
10:27:40.423  [PROBE] emitLifecycleTerminal state.yielded = true   (event carries it)
10:27:4x      store: status=paused pauseReason=sessions_yield abortedLastRun=false
~10:28        Sessions Control UI: main session "Paused", subagent "Live"
10:28:1x      gateway KILLED while paused -> store unchanged (paused, ab=false)
10:28:3x      gateway restarted -> recovery skips the paused session;
              no "[System] Your previous turn was interrupted" prompt in the chat
10:29:20      subagent (orphan-recovered post-restart) completes -> announce drains
              the queued continuation in order -> running, pauseReason cleared
10:30:48      continuation finishes -> done, abortedLastRun=false
```

Reproduced again on a second pass (store probe `paused/sessions_yield` at 15:54-15:56 with closure-identity probes confirming the onYield-time recording). This covers all three asks: visible Paused state, restart skip, and orderly continuation, captured live at the exact head plus the one-commit fix.

**Codex lane now covered too (was a sibling-lane gap, now fixed in this PR).** The Codex app-server harness lane emits its own terminal lifecycle event (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.ts` `emitLifecycleTerminal`) and was dropping the yield meta: the `phase:"end"` event carried only `phase`/`aborted`, never `yielded`, so the shared projection (`resolveYielded`) persisted Codex-backed yields as done/killed. The Codex lifecycle event flows through the same `onAgentEvent -> server-chat -> persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent -> resolveYielded` path as the native lane.

An integration test (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.yield-lifecycle.test.ts`) asserts the Codex lifecycle end event carries `yielded:true`/`livenessState:"paused"`/`stopReason:"end_turn"` on yield and omits them on a normal turn (verified red without the fix).

target.title: fix(codex): align watchdog defer guards and add wall-clock ceiling (#99272)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Codex turn watchdogs are inconsistent about when they defer:

1. **Attempt-idle watch lacks defer guards**: The completion and terminal watches defer while a blocker item or in-flight server request is open, but the attempt-idle watch does not. A long quiet native tool call (e.g., `commandExecution` with buffered output) gets hard-aborted with `turn_progress_idle_timeout`.

2. **No wall-clock ceiling**: All four watchdogs are idle-based. A wedged turn that keeps emitting unrecognized notifications never times out at the harness level.

3. **Phantom blockers from out-of-order notifications**: If `item/completed` arrives before `item/started`, the late `item/started` adds a blocker id that nothing ever removes, suppressing completion/terminal watches for the rest of the turn.

4. **Unknown methods reset idle timers**: Every current-turn notification (including methods the projector doesn't handle) resets attempt-idle timers, so unrecognized notifications can prevent timeout indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Attempt-idle + terminal watches**: Added the same defer guards (`getActiveAppServerTurnRequests() > 0` and `getActiveCompletionBlockerItemCount() > 0`) that the completion watch already has.
- **Wall-clock ceiling**: Added an absolute 60-minute wall-clock timer that fires regardless of activity, as the safety complement that makes deferring safe.
- **Blocker tracking**: `updateActiveCompletionBlockerItemIds` now accepts an optional `completedItemIds` set; late `item/started` for already-completed items is ignored.
- **Progress filtering**: Only dispatch-known notification methods count as attempt progress; unknown methods still touch completion activity but don't reset the attempt-idle watchdog.

## User Impact

- Legitimate long-running tool calls (builds, installs) are no longer aborted mid-execution.
- Wedged turns that emit only unrecognized notifications now terminate within 60 minutes instead of running forever.
- Out-of-order notification sequences no longer create phantom blockers.

## Evidence

- All 30 tests pass in `attempt-turn-watches.test.ts` (including 5 new tests)
- All 7 tests pass in `attempt-timeouts.test.ts`
- All 125 tests pass in `event-projector.test.ts`

Fixes #99272

target.title: fix: guard JSON.parse calls against malformed external responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes crashes when external data sources return malformed JSON in three locations:

1. **Docs search** — malformed API response causes unhandled `SyntaxError` in `fetchDocsSearch()` (try/finally without catch).
2. **OpenRouter music generation** — malformed SSE event data during audio streaming crashes `processOpenRouterSseLine()`.
3. **Claude MCP config** — corrupted/invalid MCP config file throws unhandled `SyntaxError` in `writeClaudeMcpCaptureConfig()`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each `JSON.parse()` processes data from an external or user-controlled source. The existing code assumed input would always be valid JSON. The fix wraps each parse in try/catch with descriptive error messages, preserves the documented CLI failure path (exit 1) for docs search, and separates filesystem errors from parse errors for MCP config.

## User Impact

- **Docs search**: malformed API response → clear `"invalid response"` error + `exit(1)`. Normal searches unaffected.
- **OpenRouter music generation**: transient SSE glitch → malformed line skipped, stream continues, valid audio decoded normally.
- **Claude MCP config**: corrupted file → `"Claude MCP config at <path> is not valid JSON"`; missing file → original `ENOENT` preserved (catch only wraps `JSON.parse`).

## Evidence

### Before/After comparison (real terminal output)

```
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  JSON.parse defensive hardening — Before/After      ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

 Scenario 1: Docs Search — malformed API response "not json at all"

   Before: raw JSON.parse
   SyntaxError — Unexpected token 'o', "not json at all" is not valid JSON
   Uncaught exception propagates to caller

   After: try/catch + descriptive error
   Docs search returned an invalid response
   Error path preserved → runtime.error() + exit(1)

 Scenario 2: OpenRouter SSE — malformed stream data

               data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"audio":{"data":"d2F2LWJ5dGVz"}}}]}
               data: [DONE]

   Before: raw JSON.parse
   SyntaxError on line 1 — audio generation aborted, valid data lost

   After: try/catch + skip
   Line 1 (invalid JSON) → skipped, stream continues
   Line 2 (valid audio) → decoded successfully
   Line 3 ([DONE]) → stream completes normally
   Result: 1 audio chunk "wav-bytes"

 Scenario 3: Claude MCP Config

   3A: Missing file
   [ENOENT] ENOENT — filesystem error preserved
   catch only wraps JSON.parse, does not mask readFile errors

   3B: Corrupted file
   Before: SyntaxError — Expected property name or '}'
   After: Claude MCP config at <path> is not valid JSON
```

target.title: fix(agents): align mid-turn tool-result projection precheck
target.body:
Refs #101929

## What Problem This Solves

Mid-turn tool-result precheck estimated the raw in-memory tool-result history, while the next provider prompt path sends the post-truncation projection. When accumulated tool results exceed the live aggregate cap, the mid-turn signal can report route/reducible-char facts from a view that the provider-boundary prompt will not actually send.

This PR now addresses only that projection mismatch. It intentionally keeps the existing conservative 2 chars/token tool-result density policy for the normal pre-prompt estimator.

## Why This Change Was Made

The mid-turn precheck now projects messages through `resolveLiveToolResultAggregateMaxChars` and `truncateOversizedToolResultsInMessages` before calling `shouldPreemptivelyCompactBeforePrompt`, using the same context-window-based aggregate cap as the provider prompt path. The global `estimateLlmBoundaryTokenPressure` tool-result density behavior is unchanged.

Risk note: this touches session-state context routing, so the tests cover the structured mid-turn signal, the aggregate-over-cap projection case, and the lower-budget overflow case where the signal must still fire.

## User Impact

Tool-heavy agent sessions with history above the provider-boundary tool-result aggregate cap should get mid-turn routing based on the same bounded prompt view used for the next model call. This does not relax token-density safety for ordinary pre-prompt compaction decisions or for tool-result histories below the projection cap.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(google): add timeout to Vertex ADC token refresh
target.body:
Related: #95865

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Google Vertex `authorized_user` Application Default Credentials token refresh can wait indefinitely when the OAuth token endpoint accepts the request but never sends a response.

## Why This Change Was Made

Vertex ADC token refresh already bounds the token response body after a response arrives, but the fetch itself had no deadline. This change adds a 30s token-refresh request timeout while preserving the existing ADC credential lookup, token cache, token-expiry handling, and bounded response-body parsing.

## User Impact

Operators using Google Vertex with local `authorized_user` ADC get a bounded authentication failure instead of a stuck provider request when the Google OAuth token refresh HTTP request stalls after connection acceptance.

## Collision / Differentiation Check

Open PRs touch the same Vertex ADC file, so this PR is intentionally narrow and differentiated:

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #97287.

When the cached `tenant_access_token` becomes invalid (e.g. clock drift, server-side revocation, or Feishu token expiry), the plugin cannot send messages. Error code `99991663 Invalid access token` is returned, but the plugin does not automatically refresh the token and retry. Users must manually restart the gateway to recover.

## Changes Made

- `extensions/feishu/src/comment-shared.ts`: Added `addFeishuTokenCacheClearer` / `clearFeishuTokenCaches`. `getFeishuTokenInvalidCode` detects 99991663/99991664. `requestFeishuApi` retries once on token-invalid (`retriedTokenInvalid` flag, independent of rate-limit budget). Fulfilled token-invalid bodies handled.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.ts`: `createFeishuClient` creates a plugin-owned `Lark.Cache` via `buildSdkTokenCache()`. `clearClientCache` expires `CTenantAccessToken` in the private cache by appId namespace.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.ts`: getter pattern — `opts.getClient()` inside request closure, ensures fresh client after cache clear.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.ts`: `clearFeishuTokenCache` registered. CardKit create retry on 99991663/99991664. Guarded-fetch release on non-JSON response.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.test.ts`: NEW — client cache isolation tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.retry.test.ts`: NEW — token-invalid + rate-limit retry sequence tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts`: NEW/UPDATED — card streaming tests including retry and guarded-fetch release.
- `extensions/feishu/src/token-retry-proof.test.ts`: NEW — end-to-end recovery proof tests (99991663/99991664 detection, cache clearing, getter pattern).

## Evidence

### 1. Production requestFeishuApi auto-retry on real 99991663 (7/7 passed)

Loads the ACTUAL `comment-shared.ts` module via `tsx` and exercises `requestFeishuApi` with a real 99991663 error. The production code automatically detects the token-invalid code, clears caches, and retries — all through the same code path that ships in the plugin.

Steering queue metadata is capped at 500 UTF-16 code units. A raw string slice could stop between an emoji's surrogate halves, leaving malformed text in the merged parent prompt.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route that boundary through the repository's canonical `truncateUtf16Safe` helper. The behavior remains unchanged for ordinary text and only backs up by one code unit when the cap would split a surrogate pair.

## User Impact

Long subagent labels, tasks, session keys, and outcome text no longer inject a dangling surrogate into the parent agent prompt.

## Scope

Two files; no config, protocol, dependency, or compatibility change. AI-assisted; maintainer-reviewed and tightened.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Steering queue metadata is capped at 500 UTF-16 code units; raw `.slice(0, 500)` could split an emoji surrogate pair, leaving malformed text in the merged parent prompt.

**Real environment tested**: Local Linux checkout at head `98d3416d49` (after merging `upstream/main` and fixing the lint nit), Node `v22.22.0`, repository `tsx`.

target.title: fix(cron): skip heartbeat-enabled checks for cron-sourced main-session wakes (#101537)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cron jobs with `sessionTarget: "main"` that deliver systemEvent payloads are skipped with `status: "skipped", error: "disabled"` when the main agent doesn't have heartbeat scheduling configured. The cron job fires on schedule but the main session is never woken.

Root cause: `runHeartbeatOnce` checks `isHeartbeatEnabledForAgent(cfg, agentId)` and `resolveHeartbeatIntervalMs()` before executing. When another agent has heartbeat configured but "main" does not, `isHeartbeatEnabledForAgent(cfg, "main")` returns false — causing the skip.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cron jobs manage their own scheduling via `CronService`. The per-agent heartbeat config and interval resolution checks are designed for the heartbeat scheduler, not for cron-sourced wakes. The fix wraps these two checks in `if (opts.source !== "cron")` so cron-sourced runs bypass them while still respecting the global `areHeartbeatsEnabled()` toggle.

## User Impact

- Cron jobs with `sessionTarget: "main"` now work correctly even when the main agent doesn't have heartbeat scheduling configured
- The global heartbeat toggle still applies — cron jobs are skipped when heartbeats are globally disabled
- No change for regular heartbeat scheduling behavior

## Evidence

- 45/45 tests pass in heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts (including 2 new regression tests)
- Format clean (oxfmt)

Fixes #101537

target.title: fix(agents): keep extension exec truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

- Keep extension/custom-tool `exec` retained stdout and stderr UTF-16 safe when output is caller-capped.
- Reuse the shared `sliceUtf16Safe` helper for both tail-retention and default output-limit truncation.
- Add regression coverage for caller-supplied caps and the default output-limit path.

## What Problem This Solves

Extension runtime commands can return stdout/stderr containing non-BMP characters such as emoji. `execCommand` retained output with `String.prototype.slice`, so a cap that landed between UTF-16 surrogate halves could return a dangling surrogate in the retained stream.

The anchor PR fixed the same class of truncation bug for exec auto-reviewer rationale text. This follow-up applies the same shared UTF-16-safe truncation invariant to extension/custom-tool command output retention.

## User Impact

Users running extensions or custom tools that emit emoji or other non-BMP text could receive broken retained stdout/stderr after truncation. That broken text can be surfaced as command output, diagnostics, or model-visible tool output. After this patch, truncation may retain one fewer UTF-16 code unit at a split boundary, but it will not return an invalid surrogate half.

## Origin / follow-up

Follows and completes #101513.

- **Anchor:** #101513 fixed exec auto-reviewer rationale truncation by using UTF-16-safe truncation.
- **Gap this fills:** `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts` still used raw `slice()` for retained stdout/stderr in the extension/custom-tool command execution path.
- **Consistency:** This patch reuses the existing `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` helper instead of introducing another truncation implementation.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

I checked current open PRs and issues for the same `execCommand` / extension exec UTF-16 truncation gap.

- No open issue matched `extension exec output UTF-16 surrogate` or `execCommand truncation surrogate`.
- No open PR matched `execCommand truncation UTF-16 safe`.
- One open PR mentions surrogate-safe truncation in a different memory-core dreaming snippet path; it does not touch `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts` or the extension exec stdout/stderr retention path.
- **Related open PR scan:** no same-file or same-runtime duplicate was found for this patch.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** extension/custom-tool exec retained stdout/stderr must not contain dangling UTF-16 surrogate halves after truncation.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** extension command output is user-triggered text that can be returned as stdout/stderr; a split surrogate can show replacement characters or invalid text to the next consumer.
- **Canonical reachability path:** user-triggered extension command output input → child-process pipe ingestion and Buffer-to-string type conversion in `execCommand` → `ExecResult` runtime object → retained stdout/stderr returned as the command effect.
- **Boundary crossed:** child-process stdout/stderr pipe payloads are captured through the same `execCommand` retention logic used by extension command execution.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** existing repository helper `sliceUtf16Safe` is reused; provider-specific constraints are not applicable to this local command-output boundary.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `appendCapturedOutput` is the source-of-truth retention boundary for `ExecResult` stdout/stderr caps. The patch fixes the invariant there instead of adding a downstream cleanup step, so stored/returned command output share the same safe retained text.
- **Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw repo on Node/Vitest using the shipped child-process output capture boundary.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/sessions/exec.test.ts
```

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module
# Imported src/agents/sessions/exec.ts, executed a child process that wrote
# A😀B to stdout and C😀D to stderr, and called execCommand(..., { maxOutputChars: 2 }).
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/sessions/exec.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  7 passed (7)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 11.57s
```

```json
{
  "stdout": "B",
  "stderr": "D",
  "stdoutLength": 1,
  "stderrLength": 1,
  "stdoutCodes": ["42"],
  "stderrCodes": ["44"],
  "stdoutDangling": [],
  "stderrDangling": [],
  "stdoutTruncatedChars": 3,
  "stderrTruncatedChars": 3,
  "code": 0
}
```

- **Observed result after fix:** stdout and stderr retain valid text with no dangling surrogate halves; truncation counts reflect the actual removed UTF-16 code units.
- **What was not tested:** full dev gateway startup was not run because the changed boundary is the local `execCommand` child-process output capture path.
- **What did NOT change:** no extension loader API, process spawning, timeout, abort, process-tree cleanup, model routing, or network behavior changed.
- **Target test file:** `src/agents/sessions/exec.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** caller-capped stdout `A😀B` and stderr `C😀D` with `maxOutputChars: 2` now retain `B` and `D` without dangling surrogate halves; the default output-limit path also avoids retaining a half emoji at the cap boundary.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** the regression hits `execCommand` at the retained-output source-of-truth boundary, covers both stdout and stderr, and also covers the default limit path where the same helper is now used.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High. The diff is limited to two slicing call sites plus focused tests, and fresh verification is bound to the committed diff.
- **Patch quality notes:** Patch quality warning considered: this is not a fallback, default-value change, catch/ignore path, or downstream masking step; it replaces unsafe slicing at the retention source.

## Review findings addressed

No maintainer review findings are attached to this follow-up yet. This patch addresses the sibling gap left by #101513 in the extension exec output retention path.

## Regression Test Plan

```bash
node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/sessions/exec.test.ts
```

The regression suite now covers:

- caller-capped retained stdout/stderr containing emoji at the truncation boundary;
- default output-limit truncation when the cap would otherwise split an emoji surrogate pair;
- existing independent stdout/stderr retention, process-tree cleanup, timeout, and stream-error behavior.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** no merge-risk label is expected for this XS scoped agents/runtime retention patch; changed files are `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts` and `src/agents/sessions/exec.test.ts` only.
- **Risk explanation:** retained output can become one UTF-16 code unit shorter at a surrogate boundary, but caps remain enforced and returned text becomes valid rather than partially split.
- **Why acceptable:** this preserves the existing API and truncation behavior while enforcing the text-validity invariant already used by the shared helper.

## Risk / Compatibility

Risk is low and localized to retained output truncation in `execCommand`.

- API shape is unchanged.
- Output caps remain enforced.
- At a surrogate boundary, retained output may be one UTF-16 code unit shorter than the raw cap to avoid returning invalid text.
- `stdoutTruncatedChars` and `stderrTruncatedChars` now count the actual number of removed UTF-16 code units after safe slicing.

## What was not changed

- No extension loader API changes.
- No process spawning, timeout, abort, or process-tree cleanup behavior changes.
- No model routing or network behavior changes.
- No new truncation helper was added.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** `execCommand` used raw `String.prototype.slice()` to enforce retained output caps. JavaScript slicing is based on UTF-16 code units, so slicing at a cap boundary can return only one half of a surrogate pair.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The fix replaces both affected slicing sites in `appendCapturedOutput` with the shared UTF-16-safe helper, covering tail retention for caller-supplied caps and head retention for default output-limit enforcement at the source where retained stdout/stderr is produced.

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary `@openclaw/lobster` `run` and `resume` calls could be routed into managed TaskFlow parsing when the tool payload contained schema-injected defaults such as `flowStateJson: "{}"` and `flowExpectedRevision: 0`.

Refs #101929

## What Problem This Solves

Mid-turn tool-result precheck estimated the raw in-memory tool-result history, while the next provider prompt path sends the post-truncation projection. When accumulated tool results exceed the live aggregate cap, the mid-turn signal can report route/reducible-char facts from a view that the provider-boundary prompt will not actually send.

This PR now addresses only that projection mismatch. It intentionally keeps the existing conservative 2 chars/token tool-result density policy for the normal pre-prompt estimator.

## Why This Change Was Made

The mid-turn precheck now projects messages through `resolveLiveToolResultAggregateMaxChars` and `truncateOversizedToolResultsInMessages` before calling `shouldPreemptivelyCompactBeforePrompt`, using the same context-window-based aggregate cap as the provider prompt path. The global `estimateLlmBoundaryTokenPressure` tool-result density behavior is unchanged.

Risk note: this touches session-state context routing, so the tests cover the structured mid-turn signal, the aggregate-over-cap projection case, and the lower-budget overflow case where the signal must still fire.

## User Impact

Tool-heavy agent sessions with history above the provider-boundary tool-result aggregate cap should get mid-turn routing based on the same bounded prompt view used for the next model call. This does not relax token-density safety for ordinary pre-prompt compaction decisions or for tool-result histories below the projection cap.

target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs
codex review --base origin/main
```

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```
openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```
node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs   # imports FIELD_HELP and buildPromptSection from this branch
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):

```
$ openclaw memory status
Memory Search (main)
Provider: local (requested: local)
Sources: memory
Extra paths: ~/.openclaw/shared-memory
Indexed: 105/105 files . 933 chunks
Workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku
By source:

```

```
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
Memory index updated (main).
```

```

[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
0.812 memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md:1-9

0.450 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md:1-6
0.432 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/pr-draft.md:1-32
```

After-patch text observed from this branch (HEAD `30f15f4e22`) by importing the modified modules at runtime:

```
$ node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs
=== schema.help.ts: FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch'] ===
Vector search over MEMORY.md and memory/**/*.md (per-agent overrides supported).

=== extensions/memory-core/index.ts (post-patch source lines) ===

```

**Observed result after fix**: (a) The freshly written nested file `memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md` (two levels deep under `memory/`) was indexed by `openclaw memory index` and returned as the top match (score `0.812`) for the unique token. A second nested hit from `memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md` (three levels deep) confirms recursion is not limited to one level. (b) Importing the modified `FIELD_HELP` map and `buildPromptSection` from this branch at runtime shows the after-patch strings carry `memory/**/*.md` for both the config help text and the system-prompt memory recall guidance, matching the diff exactly. (c) The two `memory_search` / `memory_get` description strings in `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` and `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` are inline string literals; the after-patch lines printed from this branch show the new wording in place. No runtime code paths are modified, only the descriptor and doc strings plus the regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`.

**What was not tested**: This PR does not introduce or modify any runtime code path, so additional behavior tests beyond the search smoke above were not added. The recursive walk itself (`collectMemoryFilesFromDir`) is already covered by upstream tests under `packages/memory-host-sdk/`.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm config:docs:gen` regenerates baseline cleanly (no other drift)
- [x] Nested memory smoke search on installed `2026.5.20` returns the new nested file at score `0.812`
- [x] On-branch runtime import shows `FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch']`, `buildPromptSection(...)` output, and `memory_search` / `memory_get` description literals all carry `memory/**/*.md`

- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]
```

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. target.title: fix(barnacle): resync candidate labels on ready_for_review, remove stale labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No (existing GitHub API calls)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No

- OS: any (GitHub Actions)
- Runtime/container: Node 24 (GitHub Actions)

- Integration/channel: GitHub auto-response workflow

### Steps

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body
2. Barnacle auto-labels it with `triage: blank-template`
3. Edit body to fill in the template (Problem/Why/What)
4. Click "Ready for review"

### Expected

- `triage: blank-template` is removed; correct candidate labels applied

### Actual

- `triage: blank-template` persisted (before fix)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `ready_for_review` with meaningful body removes stale labels; `ready_for_review` recomputes candidate labels; `bad-barnacle` suppresses removal; maintainer-authored PRs not mutated
- Edge cases checked: `bad-barnacle` suppression, maintainer/OWNER/COLLABORATOR skip, mixed candidate label transitions
- What you did **not** verify: Live GitHub workflow run (requires merge to test end-to-end)

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
